docs.title: Axium documentation
docs.text:
Axium is an LLM gateway you run in your own infrastructure. Your applications keep using the official OpenAI and Google SDKs; Axium sits in between, holds the provider credentials, authenticates your apps with its own API keys and records every request where you decide.

  • Getting started

    Requirements, installation with Docker, Docker Compose or on Google Cloud, and the first login.

    Install Axium

  • Configuration

    Every environment variable, the database, the license, TLS behind a reverse proxy and the web console.

    Configure

  • Observability

    Where each request is recorded: PostgreSQL, HTTP endpoints, the formats available and the exact event schema.

    Observe

  • API & SDKs

    Authentication, proxy apps, the provider gateways and ready-to-paste SDK snippets in JavaScript, Python and Java.

    Integrate

  • Operations

    Health checks, upgrades, backups, sizing and troubleshooting.

    Operate

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph yours [Your applications]
        direction TB
        A[OpenAI SDK]
        B[Google Gen AI SDK]
        C[Any HTTP client]
    end
    subgraph axium [Axium · your infrastructure]

    end

    yours -->|Bearer ax_… · native wire format| CORE

    CORE --- DB
    CORE --> O
    CORE --> G
    CORE -.->|traces| OBS[(Observability<br/>PostgreSQL · HTTP)]

docs.title: In thirty seconds
docs.text:
docker network create axium
docker run -d --name axium-db --network axium -e POSTGRES_USER=axium \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-this -e POSTGRES_DB=axium-api \
  -v axium-pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data postgres:17-alpine
docker run -d --name axium-core --network axium -p 3000:3000 \
  -e DATABASE_URL=postgresql://axium:change-this@axium-db:5432/axium-api \
  -e MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32) \
  quay.io/axiumlab/core:latest
docker run -d --name axium-ui --network axium -p 3001:3001 \
  -e API_URL=http://localhost:3000/v1 quay.io/axiumlab/ui:latest
curl http://localhost:3000/v1/install/status

Then open http://localhost:3001 and log in with admin@axium.local / admin123456. The Docker guide explains each step, and why you must keep the master key printed by that second command.

docs.title: Three things worth knowing beforehand
docs.text:
• The master key cannot be rotated. MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY encrypts the provider credentials stored in the database. If it is lost or changed, none of them can be decrypted and they all have to be entered again by hand.
  • Schema migrations run automatically and only forward. A newer image migrates an older database at startup; an older image refuses to start on a newer database. Back up before upgrading, and ask before moving up a major version.
  • If you serve the ui over HTTPS, API_URL has to be https://. The browser blocks requests to http:// from an https page without a clear error.

docs.title: API & SDKs
docs.text:
The core exposes two APIs on the same port, both under /v1/:

  • Runtime API · for your applications

    Provider-native gateways under /v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/…. Point the official OpenAI or Google SDK at them, authenticate with an ax_… key, change nothing else.

    Proxy apps & gateways · SDK examples

  • Management API · for the console and automation

    Users, roles, providers, models, proxy apps, API keys, statistics and traces. JSON, bearer tokens, role-based permissions. Everything the web console does goes through it.

    Authentication · Endpoints

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    P[Provider<br/>OpenAI · Azure OpenAI · Google AI Studio · Vertex AI] --> M[Models<br/>name · prices · scopes]
    M -->|allow-list + default| A[Proxy app<br/>status · budget · policies]
    A --> K[API keys<br/>ax_… · scoped to one app]
    K --> C[Your application]
Concept What it is Provider An account at an LLM vendor with its credentials, stored encrypted. Types: openai, azure-openai, google-aistudio, google-enterprise (Vertex AI). Model A deployed model of a provider, with input/output prices per million tokens used to compute cost. Can be global or scoped to specific apps. Proxy app The unit your applications talk to. Has an allow-list of models, a default model, a budget and a policy document (cache, firewall, DLP). States: draft → ready → inactive. API key ax_ + 40 hex. Belongs to one proxy app. Optional expiry. Gateway A path under the proxy app that speaks one vendor's protocol: /openai, /gemini, /vertex.

docs.title: Response conventions (management API)
docs.text:
{ "status": true, "data": { … }, "total": 42 }
{ "status": false, "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "…", "details": [ { "field": "name", "message": "Required" } ] } }
code HTTP VALIDATION_ERROR 400 UNAUTHORIZED 401 FORBIDDEN 403 NOT_FOUND 404 CONFLICT, LAST_SUPER_ADMIN 409 INTERNAL_ERROR 500

Malformed JSON is 400 Malformed JSON body; a body over 10 MB is 400 Request body is too large; an unknown route is 404 Route not found. Database constraint violations map to 409 Duplicate value for: <column>, 409 Record is referenced by other records or 404 Related record not found.

Errors on the runtime API are different: they are returned in the provider's own error format so SDKs can parse them. See Proxy apps & gateways.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Two kinds of credentials, for two kinds of callers.

Console users Applications Credential Bearer token obtained with email and password API key ax_… created in the console Used on Management API (/v1/users, /v1/llm, /v1/proxy-apps, …) Runtime API (/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/openai, /gemini, /vertex) Authorization Role-based permissions Scope: one proxy app Lifetime Until rotated; no expiry Optional expires_at; can be deactivated

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
curl -s http://localhost:3000/v1/users/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@axium.local","password":"admin123456"}'

{
  "status": true,
  "data": {
    "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002",
    "email": "admin@axium.local",
    "name": "Super Admin",
    "token": "9f1c…40 hex…",
    "is_active": true,
    "permissions_cache": ["core:read", "core:create", "…"],
    "last_login_at": "…", "created_at": "…", "updated_at": "…"
  }
}

Wrong credentials or an inactive user answer 401 Invalid email or password.

docs.title: Use the token
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:3000/v1/users/me -H "Authorization: Bearer 9f1c…"

The token is opaque (not a JWT) and validated against the database on every request. It has no expiry. A new one is issued, invalidating the previous, on every login, on POST /v1/users/logout, when the account is deactivated and when an administrator resets the password.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Each route declares the permissions that open it; the user needs at least one. Without a valid token: 401 Unauthorized. With a token but without the permission: 403 Forbidden. The list of permissions a user holds comes back in permissions_cache at login and in GET /v1/users/me.

Permissions are module:action:

Modules Actions core (users, roles), llm (providers, models), rm (proxy apps, API keys, projects), observability (stats, traces), governance, chat, mcp, agents read, view, create, update, delete, manage, execute, test, export

The seeded super-admin role holds all of them. Create narrower roles with POST /v1/roles and PATCH /v1/roles/:id/permissions.

docs.title: Change the initial password
docs.text:
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/v1/users/password \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"current_password":"admin123456","new_password":"a-long-new-password"}'

Minimum 8 characters.

docs.title: Create one
docs.text:
In the console, or:

curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/v1/rm/api-keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <console token>" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"billing-service","scope_type":"proxy_app","proxy_app_id":"<app-id>","expires_at":"2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"}'

The response contains key in clear once. Axium stores only a hash and the last four characters; a lost key has to be replaced.

docs.title: Send it
docs.text:
Either header works; Authorization wins if both are present:

Authorization: Bearer ax_8d2d9ff993e24eb6144e8d87e7890a51401eca99
x-goog-api-key: ax_8d2d9ff993e24eb6144e8d87e7890a51401eca99

The second exists so Google's SDKs work unchanged. A ?key= query parameter is not accepted and is stripped before forwarding.

docs.title: What the runtime checks
docs.text:
1. The key exists, is active and has not expired. Any failure is the same 401, on purpose.
  2. The key is scoped to a proxy app, and it is the app in the URL. Otherwise 403.
  3. From there, the proxy app's own rules apply: status, budget, model allow-list, policies. See Proxy apps & gateways.

last_used_at is updated on a best-effort basis.

docs.title: Rotate
docs.text: Create the new key, deploy it, then deactivate the old one with PATCH /v1/rm/api-keys/:id {"is_active": false}. Deactivating keeps the key's history in statistics and traces; deleting does too but loses its name.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Management API reference. All routes are under /v1, take and return JSON, and require Authorization: Bearer <console token> unless marked public. The last column is the permission needed (any one of them, when several are listed).
