docs.title: Projects and endpoints (preview)
docs.text: /rm/projects and /rm/endpoints offer CRUD for a prompt-management feature whose runtime is not yet available. API keys with scope_type: rm_project can be created but have nothing to call. Expect these routes to change.

docs.title: Runtime API
docs.text: The provider gateways under /proxy-apps/:proxyAppId/{openai,gemini,vertex} are documented in Proxy apps & gateways.

docs.title: Proxy apps & gateways
docs.text:
A proxy app is the thing your application talks to. Each one exposes the provider protocols as gateways under its URL:

https://<core>/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/openai/…    OpenAI protocol
https://<core>/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/gemini/…    Gemini API protocol
https://<core>/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/vertex/…    Vertex AI protocol

Axium does not translate between protocols. The body you send goes to the provider as-is; the only edits are the model field (replaced by the deployed model name) and, for streamed chat completions, stream_options.include_usage = true so usage can be recorded (your client receives one extra chunk with an empty choices array). Provider errors come back verbatim.

docs.title: OpenAI gateway
docs.text:
Prefix /openai or /openai/v1. Serves openai and azure-openai providers, and any provider whose models speak the OpenAI protocol.

Method Path Surface Streaming POST chat/completions openai.chat yes POST responses openai.responses yes GET models, models/:model openai.models POST files (multipart, forwarded intact; openai providers only) openai.files GET files, files/:id, files/:id/content (text only) openai.files DELETE files/:id openai.files

Not available: /embeddings, /images, /audio, /batches, /uploads.

docs.title: Gemini gateway
docs.text:
Prefixes /gemini, /gemini/v1, /gemini/v1beta. Serves google-aistudio and google-enterprise providers.

Method Path Surface Streaming POST models/:model:generateContent gemini.generate POST models/:model:streamGenerateContent (?alt=sse optional) gemini.generate yes POST models/:model:countTokens (not billed) and other verbs gemini.generate GET models, models/:model gemini.models POST interactions (model or agent) gemini.interactions yes GET interactions/:id (?stream=true) gemini.interactions yes POST / DELETE interactions/:id/cancel, interactions/:id gemini.interactions POST /gemini/upload/v1beta/files, /gemini/upload/v1/files (resumable, 2 steps; google-aistudio only) gemini.files GET / DELETE files, files/:id gemini.files

OpenAI-compatible facade (google-aistudio only): POST /gemini[/v1|/v1beta]/openai/chat/completions, GET …/openai/models, GET …/openai/models/:model. Lets the OpenAI SDK talk to Gemini models by changing its base URL. No Responses API on this facade.

Resumable uploads return an upload URL for the second step. Set PUBLIC_BASE_URL (and TRUST_PROXY) behind TLS so that URL points back through Axium with the right scheme.

docs.title: Vertex AI gateway
docs.text:
Prefix /vertex, /vertex/v1 or /vertex/v1beta1. Serves google-enterprise providers only.

POST /vertex/v1/projects/:project/locations/:location/publishers/:publisher/models/:model:generateContent
POST …:streamGenerateContent        (streaming)
POST …:countTokens                  (not billed)
  • :project is ignored; the proxy app is what gets billed and the provider's configured project is what gets called.
  • :location (^[a-z0-9-]+$) decides the Google region. global works.
  • :publisher/:model becomes the model name, e.g. google/gemini-2.5-flash or anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5.
  • There is no model catalogue under /vertex/…/publishers/:publisher/models.

docs.title: Not supported
docs.text: No Anthropic Messages dialect (/v1/messages), no embeddings, image or audio endpoints, no OpenAI Uploads API for files over 512 MB. Methods accepted on the gateways: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE.

docs.title: Request pipeline
docs.text:
Every runtime request goes through these checks, in order. The first failure ends the request with the HTTP status shown and a trace with that denial_reason (schema).

flowchart TD
    A[API key valid · scoped to this app] -->|401 / 403| X((deny))
    A --> B[Streaming supported on this surface]
    B --> C[firewall.inbound · client IP]
    C --> D[App exists · status ready]
    D --> E[Budget for the current period]
    E --> F[Model allowed · unambiguous · provider active · protocol matches]
    F --> G[dlp_prompt · mask or block]
    G --> H{cache strict?}
    H -->|hit| R[200 · x-axium-cache: hit]
    H -->|miss / off| P[Forward to provider]
    P --> S[Record usage · emit trace]

docs.title: Models and defaults
docs.text:
• A proxy app sees the models in its allow-list plus models marked global. Manage with PATCH /v1/proxy-apps/:id/allowed-models.
  • The client may name a model ("model": "gpt-4o-mini") or omit it and get the app's default model (PATCH /v1/proxy-apps/:id/default-models). Omitting it on a surface where the SDK requires it still needs a placeholder; Axium ignores the value only when the app resolves a default.
  • A name matching more than one allowed model is 400 model_ambiguous; one matching none is 403 model_not_allowed.
  • A fallback model can be configured but is not used by the runtime in this version.

docs.title: Budget
docs.text:
Field Meaning budget_limit Decimal, in the currency of the model prices. budget_period daily, weekly, monthly or null. Calendar windows evaluated in the database's time zone. null = a lifetime budget that never resets.

When the app's spend in the current window reaches the limit, requests are refused with 429 and denial_reason = budget_exhausted. The counter resets lazily on the first charge of the next window. Spend is computed from token usage and model prices; models without prices do not count.

rate_limit_rpm and rate_limit_tpm exist on apps and models and are stored but not enforced in this version. Put rate limiting at your ingress if you need it.

docs.title: Policies
docs.text: Each proxy app carries a JSON policy document, validated on PATCH /v1/proxy-apps/:id (a 400 lists each invalid field with a stable code).

docs.title: cache
docs.text:
{ "cache": { "mode": "strict", "ttl_seconds": 3600 } }
mode Behaviour off Default. strict Exact-match cache keyed on an MD5 of the canonicalised body plus the requested model, per app and model. Hits answer 200 with x-axium-cache: hit, no tokens, no cost, no provider call. semantic Accepted but not implemented; behaves as off.

Only non-streamed generations without previous_response_id / previous_interaction_id are cached, and only successful JSON responses. Entries live in rm.request_io; expired rows are removed with DELETE /v1/proxy-apps/:id/cache/expired or the global DELETE /v1/proxy-apps/cache/expired.

docs.title: firewall
docs.text:
{
  "firewall": {
    "inbound": {
      "default_action": "deny",
      "rules": [
        { "action": "allow", "type": "cidr", "value": "10.0.0.0/8" },
        { "action": "allow", "type": "cidr", "value": "203.0.113.0/24" }
      ]
    }
  }
}

First matching rule wins; up to 256 rules. An unknown client IP (no TRUST_PROXY behind a proxy) falls to default_action. Denials are 403 firewall_denied. The outbound section is stored but not applied.

docs.title: dlp_prompt
docs.text:
{
  "dlp_prompt": {
    "enabled": true,
    "options": {
      "countries": ["ES", "FR", "DE"],
      "policy": {
        "default": "mask",
        "kinds": { "financial": "block" },
        "entities": { "EMAIL": "keep" }
      }
    }
  }
}

Scans the prompt (instructions, user text) for personal identifiers using @axium-lab/euro-pii. Per kind or per entity:

Action Effect mask The value is replaced in the forwarded body by <ENTITY>. Binary and URL parts are left alone. block 403 with denial_reason = dlp_blocked and message Request contains data this proxy app does not allow. keep Forwarded unchanged; the finding is still recorded.

If scanning fails the request proceeds and the trace notes action: error. Findings (entity names and kinds, never values) land in attributes.dlp_prompt of the trace. dlp_file and capture sections are accepted but not applied in this version.

docs.title: Request headers Axium reads
docs.text:
Header Goes to Authorization: Bearer ax_… or x-goog-api-key: ax_… Authentication x-axium-user-id trace client_user_id x-axium-meta-tag trace meta_tag x-axium-<anything> trace tags.<anything>

No x-axium-* header is forwarded. Also stripped before forwarding: authorization, x-goog-api-key, api-key, x-api-key, cookie, host, hop-by-hop headers, and the key query parameter.

docs.title: Response headers Axium adds
docs.text:
Header When x-axium-trace-id Always. The trace's id; log it on the client to correlate. x-axium-cache: hit Served from cache. content-type: text/event-stream, cache-control: no-cache, x-accel-buffering: no Streaming responses.

Removed from provider responses: connection, content-encoding, content-length, keep-alive, transfer-encoding.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Provider errors are relayed verbatim with their status. Errors Axium generates are encoded in the gateway's dialect (OpenAI or Gemini error JSON) with these statuses:

Category HTTP invalid_request, content_filter 400 auth_error 401 permission_denied 403 not_found 404 rate_limit, quota_exceeded 429 server_error, unknown 500 timeout 504

Every error carries an x-axium-trace-id; the trace has error_origin, error_category, error_message and, when Axium refused the request, denial_reason.

docs.title: Lifecycle of a proxy app
docs.text:
# 1. create (status: draft)
POST /v1/proxy-apps            {"name":"billing-assistant","description":"…"}
# 2. allow models and pick a default
PATCH /v1/proxy-apps/:id/allowed-models   {"model_ids":["…"]}
PATCH /v1/proxy-apps/:id/default-models   {…}
# 3. budget and policies
PATCH /v1/proxy-apps/:id       {"budget_limit":100,"budget_period":"monthly","policies":{…}}
# 4. publish (status: ready) and create a key
PATCH /v1/proxy-apps/:id/publish
POST  /v1/rm/api-keys          {"name":"prod","scope_type":"proxy_app","proxy_app_id":":id"}
# later
PATCH /v1/proxy-apps/:id/deactivate       # 403 app_not_ready for every caller
GET   /v1/proxy-apps/:id/stats?from=…&to=…

docs.title: SDK examples
docs.text:
Axium exposes each provider's native wire protocol under a proxy app, so you keep using the official SDKs and only change two things: the base URL and the API key. The examples below are taken from the examples/ folder of this repository and run against a local core on http://localhost:3000.

Replace <app-id> with your proxy app id and ax_… with an API key created in the console. See Proxy apps & gateways for the URL layout and Authentication for the key format.

docs.title: OpenAI SDK
docs.text:
The OpenAI gateway lives at …/proxy-apps/<app-id>/openai. The SDK appends /responses, /chat/completions, /files, … to it.

JavaScriptPythoncurl 
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: 'ax_…',
  baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/openai',
});

const response = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'gpt-4o-mini',
  input: 'Name three colours',
});
console.log(response.output_text);

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="ax_…",
    base_url="http://localhost:3000/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/openai",
)

response = client.responses.create(model="gpt-4o-mini", input="Name three colours")
print(response.output_text)

curl http://localhost:3000/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/openai/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ax_…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"Name three colours"}'

Structured outputs (text.format with a JSON schema), tool calls, streaming and file uploads work exactly as against OpenAI. The examples/sdk-js/openai.js file in the repository exercises each of them.

docs.title: Google Gen AI SDK (Gemini API)
docs.text:
The Gemini gateway lives at …/proxy-apps/<app-id>/gemini. The SDK appends /v1beta/models/<model>:<verb>.

Authentication header

Google's SDK sends the key as x-goog-api-key, which Axium accepts, so apiKey: 'ax_…' is enough. Adding Authorization: Bearer ax_… as a default header is harmless and makes the intent explicit; if both are present, Authorization wins.

JavaScriptPython 
import { GoogleGenAI } from '@google/genai';

const ai = new GoogleGenAI({
  apiKey: 'ax_…',
  httpOptions: {
    baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3000/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/gemini',
    headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ax_…' },
  },
});

const response = await ai.models.generateContent({
  model: 'gemini-2.5-flash',
  contents: 'Name three colours',
});
console.log(response.text);

from google import genai
from google.genai import types

client = genai.Client(
    api_key="ax_…",
    http_options=types.HttpOptions(
        base_url="http://localhost:3000/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/gemini",
        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer ax_…"},
    ),
)

response = client.models.generate_content(model="gemini-2.5-flash", contents="Name three colours")
print(response.text)

docs.title: Google Gen AI SDK (Vertex AI)
docs.text:
The Vertex gateway lives at …/proxy-apps/<app-id>/vertex. The SDK builds /v1beta1/projects/<project>/locations/<location>/publishers/<publisher>/models/<model>:<verb> on top of it.

Two things to know:

  • project is ignored. Axium replaces it with the project configured in the provider. Any value works.
  • location counts. It decides the Google region the request is sent to (global, europe-west1, …).
  • Model names are publisher models. google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite becomes publishers/google/models/gemini-2.5-flash-lite. Without a slash the SDK assumes publishers/google.
JavaScriptJava (google-genai)Java (LangChain4j)Java (Spring AI) 
import { GoogleGenAI } from '@google/genai';

const ai = new GoogleGenAI({
  vertexai: true,
  project: 'ignored-by-axium',
  location: 'global',
  apiKey: 'ax_…',          // keeps the SDK away from ADC
  httpOptions: {
    baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3000/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/vertex',
  },
});

const response = await ai.models.generateContent({
  model: 'google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite',
  contents: 'Which model are you?',
  config: { seed: 42 },
});
console.log(response.text);

In Java .apiKey() is mutually exclusive with .project()/.location(), and with only .apiKey() the SDK enters Vertex express mode and changes the path to /v1/publishers/google/models/…, which the proxy answers with 404 Route not found. Pass the key as a static credential instead: it is sent as Authorization: Bearer ax_… and never refreshed.

import com.google.auth.oauth2.AccessToken;
import com.google.auth.oauth2.GoogleCredentials;
import com.google.genai.Client;
import com.google.genai.types.HttpOptions;

Client ai = Client.builder()
    .vertexAI(true)
    .project("ignored-by-axium")
    .location("global")
    .credentials(GoogleCredentials.create(new AccessToken("ax_…", null)))
    .httpOptions(HttpOptions.builder()
        .baseUrl("https://axium-api.your-domain.com/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/vertex")
        .build())
    .build();

var response = ai.models.generateContent("google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite", "Which model are you?", null);
System.out.println(response.text());

.apiEndpoint() accepts the full proxy URL, host and path, so no manual client is needed:

GoogleGenAiChatModel model = GoogleGenAiChatModel.builder()
    .googleCredentials(GoogleCredentials.create(new AccessToken("ax_…", null)))
    .projectId("ignored-by-axium")
    .location("global")
    .apiEndpoint("https://axium-api.your-domain.com/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/vertex")
    .modelName("google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite")
    .build();

Use the spring-ai-google-genai module (not the starter) and build the com.google.genai.Client yourself as in the google-genai tab, then hand it to GoogleGenAiChatModel. If you prefer the starter, set spring.ai.model.chat=none so its auto-configured model does not try ADC. ChatOptions does not expose seed.

Complete, runnable Docker projects for the three Java variants are in examples/vertex-java/.

docs.title: OpenAI SDK against Gemini (OpenAI-compatible facade)
docs.text:
Google AI Studio serves its models in OpenAI format under /v1beta/openai. Axium exposes the same facade inside the Gemini gateway for google-aistudio providers, so the OpenAI SDK only changes its base URL:

import OpenAI from 'openai';

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: 'ax_…',
  baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000/v1/proxy-apps/<app-id>/gemini/v1beta/openai',
});

const r = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'gemini-2.5-flash',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Name three colours' }],
});
console.log(r.choices[0].message.content);

This facade exposes chat.completions and models only; there is no Responses API on it.

docs.title: Running the repository examples
docs.text:
cd examples/sdk-js
npm install
node openai.js 1      # test number, see the file for the list
node gemini.js 2
node vertex.js 3

The Java examples each have a Dockerfile; no local Java or Maven needed:

cd examples/vertex-java/java-google-genai
docker build -t genai-test . && docker run --rm genai-test

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Axium is configured entirely through environment variables. The images carry no configuration files and no .env; what you pass to the container is the whole configuration.

  • Environment variables

    Every variable the core reads, with defaults, validation rules and what happens when a value is missing or invalid.

    Reference

  • Database

    Connection string, supported versions, schemas, pool sizes and the automatic schema installation and migration.

    Database

  • License

    How the license is loaded, validated and renewed.

    License

  • Reverse proxy & TLS

    TRUST_PROXY, PUBLIC_BASE_URL and example configurations for nginx, Caddy and Traefik.

    Reverse proxy

  • Web console (ui)

    The one variable the ui needs and the mistakes everyone makes with it.

    Ui

  • Security

    Encryption at rest, credentials, sessions, API keys, CORS and what to lock down at the ingress.

    Security

docs.title: Minimal and recommended configurations
docs.text:
Minimal (evaluation)Recommended (production) 
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://axium:secret@db:5432/axium-api
MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<64 hex>

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://axium:secret@db:5432/axium-api
MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<64 hex>
AXIUM_LICENSE=<40 hex>

# Behind a TLS-terminating proxy or load balancer
TRUST_PROXY=true
PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://axium-api.your-domain.com

# Record every request
OBSERVABILITY_TYPE=postgres
OBSERVABILITY_DB_POSTGRESQL=postgresql://axium:secret@db:5432/axium-api

# Optional
LOG_REQUESTS=true
MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE=50mb

docs.title: Database
docs.text: PostgreSQL holds everything Axium persists: users, roles, providers and their encrypted credentials, models, proxy apps, API keys, the response cache and daily statistics. The core and the ui keep no state of their own.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://axium:secret@axium-db:5432/axium-api
Pool per core instance min 0, max 10 connections Startup wait up to 30 s, one SELECT 1 per second, then the process exits TLS whatever the DSN says (?sslmode=require); the driver is pg

Multiply the pool maximum by the number of core replicas (plus 8 per replica if the PostgreSQL observability destination points to the same server) and make sure max_connections on the server allows it with headroom.

docs.title: Cloud SQL and other Unix sockets
docs.text:
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://axium:secret@localhost/axium-api?host=/cloudsql/PROJECT:REGION:INSTANCE

The localhost authority is mandatory filler: the connection goes through the socket in host=, but a DSN with an empty authority makes the driver fall back to a different database engine and silently try localhost:5432.

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL 17 is what development and CI run against, and what the installers deploy.
  • The schema needs PostgreSQL 13 or newer: native gen_random_uuid(), GENERATED ALWAYS AS … STORED columns, GROUPING SETS, INET, JSONB with GIN indexes and transaction-level advisory locks.
  • No extensions are required. No pgcrypto, no uuid-ossp.

Managed services (Cloud SQL, RDS, Azure Database, Neon, Supabase, …) work as long as the user can create schemas in the database.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
The user in DATABASE_URL must be able to:

  • CREATE SCHEMA in the database (GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE "axium-api" TO axium;)
  • create tables, types, functions and triggers in those schemas

It creates the schemas core, llm, rm and stats. With OBSERVABILITY_TYPE=postgres it also creates telemetry in whichever database OBSERVABILITY_DB_POSTGRESQL points to.

docs.title: Schema installation
docs.text:
On every start, after connecting, the core checks the schema and acts on what it finds:

State Meaning Action not_installed No Axium schema at all Installs the complete schema in one transaction and seeds the super-admin role and the admin@axium.local user. Log: [install] schema version N installed. installed, current version Normal case Nothing. Log: [install] schema version N is current. installed, older version Image newer than the database Applies the bundled migrations one version at a time, each in its own transaction. Log: [install] schema migrated 1 -> 3. A failed migration exits the process rather than serve an unknown schema. installed, newer version Database newer than the image Exits with The database is at schema version N but this build ships M. Update the API to the latest version. partial Axium schemas exist but no version table Refuses to touch it. Logs the failure and keeps running so /v1/install/status can be queried. Needs a human.

Installation and migrations take a transaction-level advisory lock, so several replicas can start at the same time against an empty database and only one installs.

A failed first installation does not stop the process: the routes come up and almost everything answers a database error. That is why /v1/install/status, not /v1/health, is the check that matters. See Health checks.

docs.title: Checking the version
docs.text:
curl -s http://localhost:3000/v1/install/status
# {"status":true,"data":{"state":"installed","version":3}}

Or, authenticated, GET /v1/diagnostics, which also reports the version the running build expects.

docs.title: Manual installation
docs.text: POST /v1/install installs the schema on demand when the state is not_installed. It answers 409 CONFLICT once installed and 500 on a partial database. Both /v1/install routes are public and stay open forever, so restrict them at the ingress after installing; see Security.

docs.title: Time zone matters
docs.text:
Daily statistics use CURRENT_DATE and budget windows use date_trunc('day' | 'week' | 'month', now()), both evaluated with the PostgreSQL server's time zone. Set it deliberately:

ALTER DATABASE "axium-api" SET timezone TO 'UTC';

docs.title: Housekeeping the core does not do
docs.text:
• Response cache. rm.request_io keeps one row per (proxy app, request hash) when the cache policy is strict. Expired rows are not purged automatically; use DELETE /v1/proxy-apps/cache/expired or DELETE /v1/proxy-apps/:id/cache/expired from a cron job.
  • Traces. telemetry.proxy_traces has no retention. See PostgreSQL destination.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text: See Backup & restore. Remember that a database backup is only usable together with the MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY it was written under.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
The core reads its configuration from environment variables at startup. There are two groups with different failure behaviour:

  • Core variables are validated strictly. A missing required value or an invalid one aborts the start with a message naming the variable.
  • Observability variables never abort. An invalid value prints an error prefixed [observability] and leaves observability disabled for the life of the process.

Legend: required optional

docs.title: DATABASE_URL required
docs.text:
PostgreSQL connection string.

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://axium:secret@axium-db:5432/axium-api

No default. The format is not validated beyond being a non-empty string; a wrong DSN shows up as [db] waiting for postgres... for 30 seconds followed by a crash. For a Cloud SQL Unix socket use postgresql://user:pass@localhost/dbname?host=/cloudsql/<connectionName> (the localhost is mandatory filler). See Database.

docs.title: MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY required
docs.text:
Key used to encrypt provider credentials at rest with AES-256-GCM.

  • Format: exactly 64 hexadecimal characters (32 bytes). Anything else aborts with must be 64 hex characters (32 bytes). A trailing newline counts as a character.
  • Generate: openssl rand -hex 32
  • Cannot be rotated. Changing it makes every stored provider credential undecryptable; each provider has to be re-created or edited with its credentials again. Back it up with the database.

docs.title: PORT optional
docs.text: Listening port. Default 3000. Must be an integer between 0 and 65535. Platforms such as Cloud Run inject it for you.

docs.title: NODE_ENV optional
docs.text: One of development, test, production. The image sets production. Any other value aborts. Its only effect is the default of LOG_REQUESTS.

docs.title: LOG_REQUESTS optional
docs.text:
true writes one line per HTTP request to stdout:

[req] POST /v1/proxy-apps/…/openai/v1/chat/completions 200 843ms
[req] POST /v1/proxy-apps/…/openai/v1/chat/completions 200 12043ms (aborted)

Default: on when NODE_ENV=development, off otherwise. An explicit value wins. Malformed JSON requests are logged too. See Request logging.

docs.title: MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE optional
docs.text:
Ceiling for the body of a file upload request. Default 50mb. Accepts bytes-style strings: 10mb, 2gb, 524288000.

  • Applies only to the upload routes: …/openai/files, …/openai/v1/files, …/gemini/upload/v1beta/files, …/gemini/upload/v1/files.
  • The whole upload is held in RAM for the duration of the request. Size the container accordingly, or lower this value.
  • An empty string is not the default: it removes the limit entirely.
  • JSON bodies have a separate, fixed limit of 10 MB that is not configurable.

docs.title: TRUST_PROXY optional
docs.text:
true makes the core trust X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto from the hop in front of it. Default false.

Set it to true only when a reverse proxy or load balancer terminates TLS in front of the core. It affects:

  • the client IP seen by the firewall policy and recorded as client_ip in traces;
  • the protocol used to rewrite Gemini resumable-upload URLs.

With false and a proxy in front, every client looks like the proxy. With true and no proxy, a client can forge its IP. See Reverse proxy & TLS.

docs.title: PUBLIC_BASE_URL optional
docs.text:
Public URL of the core, e.g. https://axium-api.your-domain.com. No default.

Used for one thing: rewriting the x-goog-upload-url header that Google returns in the first step of a Gemini resumable upload, so the second step also goes through Axium. When unset, the core builds the URL from the request (protocol://host), which is only wrong when something in front terminates TLS. A trailing slash is removed.

docs.title: AXIUM_LICENSE optional
docs.text: Your license key, 40 hexadecimal characters. Validated once at startup against the Axium Lab license service. Today an absent or invalid license is only logged; the process starts anyway. See License.

docs.title: AXIUM_LICENSE_FILE optional
docs.text:
Path to a JSON file holding the license, read only when AXIUM_LICENSE is empty. Default /license/license.json. Format:

{ "license": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567" }

A missing file means "no license". A file without a non-empty license string logs an error. Intended for mounting the key as a secret volume.

docs.title: AXIUM_METASERVER optional
docs.text: Base URL of the Axium Lab metadata service. Default https://meta.axium-lab.com/v1. Must be a valid URL or the start aborts. Used for GET {base}/license/check/{key} and POST {base}/telemetry. Only change it if Axium Lab gives you a different endpoint.

docs.title: TELEMETRY_ENABLED optional
docs.text:
Default true. Once per process start (never periodically) the core sends one anonymous usage snapshot to the metadata service. It never blocks or fails the start, and nothing is sent when the schema is not installed.

TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false
What the snapshot contains

Aggregates over the whole history of the installation, no names, no prompts, no money:

{
  "telemetry_schema": 1,
  "install_id": "<random uuid generated at install>",
  "app_version": "3.1.0",
  "schema_version": 3,
  "installed_at": "…", "sent_at": "…",
  "traffic": {
    "requests": 0, "errors": 0, "denied": 0, "streamed": 0,
    "tokens_in": 0, "tokens_out": 0, "tokens_cached": 0,
    "tokens_reasoning": 0, "tokens_saved": 0,
    "avg_latency_ms": null, "max_latency_ms": null, "avg_ttfb_ms": null
  },
  "coverage": { "first_day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "last_day": "YYYY-MM-DD" }
}

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: These select and configure the per-request trace destination. The full behaviour is in the Observability section.

docs.title: OBSERVABILITY_TYPE optional
docs.text:
Value Effect unset, empty, none Traces are not recorded. Default. postgres Traces are written to a PostgreSQL database and readable through the API. http Traces are POSTed in batches to an HTTP endpoint.

Any other value logs unknown OBSERVABILITY_TYPE "<x>" (expected: postgres, http), disabled.

docs.title: OBSERVABILITY_DB_POSTGRESQL required with postgres
docs.text: Connection string of the database that receives the traces. It can be the main Axium database or a separate one. Empty with OBSERVABILITY_TYPE=postgres disables observability with a log line. The core opens a separate pool for it (max 8 connections).

docs.title: OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_URL required with http
docs.text: URL that receives one POST per batch. Not probed at startup: a wrong URL shows up on the first flush as a throttled error log.

docs.title: OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_FORMAT optional
docs.text: envelope (default) or ndjson. See Formats & event schema.

docs.title: OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_HEADERS optional
docs.text:
A flat JSON object of string headers added to every POST, typically for authentication:

OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_HEADERS='{"Authorization":"Bearer xxx"}'
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_HEADERS='{"DD-API-KEY":"…"}'

They are applied after Axium's own headers, so they can override content-type and x-axium-trace-version. Anything that is not a JSON object of strings disables observability with a log line.

docs.title: Variables that do not exist
docs.text: To save you a search: there is no configuration for CORS (it is open, see Security), rate limiting, provider timeouts or retries, log level or JSON logging, JWT secrets, OpenTelemetry (OTEL_*), Langfuse or feature flags. API_URL belongs to the ui, not the core; see Web console.

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text: Variable Required Default Invalid value DATABASE_URL yes — aborts MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY yes — aborts PORT no 3000 aborts NODE_ENV no production (image) aborts LOG_REQUESTS no off in production aborts MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE no 50mb aborts TRUST_PROXY no false aborts PUBLIC_BASE_URL no request host — AXIUM_LICENSE no — logged AXIUM_LICENSE_FILE no /license/license.json logged AXIUM_METASERVER no https://meta.axium-lab.com/v1 aborts TELEMETRY_ENABLED no true aborts OBSERVABILITY_TYPE no off observability disabled OBSERVABILITY_DB_POSTGRESQL with postgres — observability disabled OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_URL with http — observability disabled OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_FORMAT no envelope observability disabled OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_HEADERS no {} observability disabled

docs.title: License
docs.text: Every installation runs under an Axium license: a key of 40 hexadecimal characters that Axium Lab gives you.

docs.title: Providing it
docs.text:
Environment variableFile (secret volume)Google Cloud installer 
AXIUM_LICENSE=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

Leave AXIUM_LICENSE unset and mount a JSON file at /license/license.json (or point AXIUM_LICENSE_FILE elsewhere):

{ "license": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567" }

docker run … -v /secure/license.json:/license/license.json:ro quay.io/axiumlab/core:latest

gcp.sh asks for the license, validates it before creating anything and stores it in the AXIUM_LICENSE variable of the axium-core service. Pass AXIUM_LICENSE=… in the environment to skip the prompt.

docs.title: What happens at startup
docs.text:
1. The core calls GET https://meta.axium-lab.com/v1/license/check/<key> (base URL configurable with AXIUM_METASERVER).
  2. The service answers with a signed token (JWT, EdDSA/Ed25519). The core verifies the signature against a public key embedded in the binary, and checks that the product is axium, that the license is valid and that it has not expired.

  3. It logs one of:

    [license] valid — Acme Corp (enterprise), expires 2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
[license] invalid — license is expired
[license] no license configured

The check happens once per process start. There is no periodic re-check.

Enforcement

In the current version an absent or invalid license is logged, not enforced: the process starts and serves traffic. Treat the log line as the signal that something needs fixing before a future version starts enforcing it.

If the license service is unreachable the check fails with a network error in the log and the core starts normally.

docs.title: Checking a key yourself
docs.text:
curl -s https://meta.axium-lab.com/v1/license/check/<key> | jq

A valid key answers {"status":true,"data":{"license":"<jwt>"}}. The token's payload (second base64url segment) carries customer_name, type, features, expires_at and revoked_at.

docs.title: Renewing
docs.text:
Replace the value and restart the core. On Cloud Run:

gcloud run services update axium-core --region europe-west1 \
  --update-env-vars AXIUM_LICENSE=<new key>

No reinstall, no data change.

docs.title: Reverse proxy & TLS
docs.text: Axium does not terminate TLS. In anything beyond a laptop, put a reverse proxy or a load balancer in front of both the core and the ui and let it hold the certificates.

docs.title: What the core needs from the proxy
docs.text:
Setting Value Why TRUST_PROXY true So the core reads the real client IP and protocol from X-Forwarded-For / X-Forwarded-Proto. Without it the firewall policy and the client_ip trace column see the proxy's address. PUBLIC_BASE_URL https://axium-api.your-domain.com Only matters for Gemini resumable uploads; otherwise the upload URL handed to the client would be http://. Request body size ≥ MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE (default 50 MB) Otherwise the proxy rejects uploads before Axium sees them. Read/response timeout several minutes LLM generations can take minutes; streaming keeps the connection open for the whole answer. Response buffering off Streaming (text/event-stream) must reach the client chunk by chunk. The core already sends X-Accel-Buffering: no and Cache-Control: no-cache. HTTP/1.1 keep-alive to upstream on Cheaper connections, correct SSE behaviour.

The ui needs nothing special; it serves static files. What matters is that its API_URL is the public HTTPS URL of the core, see Web console.

docs.title: Example: nginx
docs.text:
server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name axium-api.your-domain.com;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/ssl/axium/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/axium/privkey.pem;

    client_max_body_size 50m;          # match MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE

    location / {
        proxy_pass         http://axium-core:3000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header   Host              $host;
        proxy_set_header   X-Forwarded-For   $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header   X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_set_header   Connection        "";

        proxy_buffering    off;          # streaming
        proxy_read_timeout 600s;
        proxy_send_timeout 600s;
    }

    # Lock the installer down once installed (see Security)
    location /v1/install {
        allow 10.0.0.0/8;
        deny  all;
        proxy_pass http://axium-core:3000;
    }
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name axium.your-domain.com;
    ssl_certificate     /etc/ssl/axium/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/axium/privkey.pem;
    location / { proxy_pass http://axium-ui:3001; }
}

docs.title: Example: Caddy
docs.text:
axium-api.your-domain.com {
    request_body { max_size 50MB }
    reverse_proxy axium-core:3000 {
        flush_interval -1          # streaming
        transport http { response_header_timeout 10m }
    }
}

axium.your-domain.com {
    reverse_proxy axium-ui:3001
}

Caddy sets X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto by default and obtains certificates automatically.

docs.title: Example: Traefik (Docker labels)
docs.text:
services:
  core:
    image: quay.io/axiumlab/core:v0.1.0
    environment:
      TRUST_PROXY: "true"
      PUBLIC_BASE_URL: https://axium-api.your-domain.com
    labels:
      traefik.enable: "true"
      traefik.http.routers.axium-core.rule: Host(`axium-api.your-domain.com`)
      traefik.http.routers.axium-core.tls.certresolver: letsencrypt
      traefik.http.services.axium-core.loadbalancer.server.port: "3000"
      traefik.http.middlewares.axium-body.buffering.maxRequestBodyBytes: "52428800"
      traefik.http.routers.axium-core.middlewares: axium-body

Traefik does not buffer responses by default, which is what streaming needs.

docs.title: Cloud Run
docs.text: The Google Cloud installer already sets TRUST_PROXY=true because Cloud Run terminates TLS and always rewrites the X-Forwarded-* headers. Cloud Run's request timeout defaults to 5 minutes; raise it with gcloud run services update axium-core --timeout=900 if you expect longer generations.

docs.title: Mixed content
docs.text: If the ui is served over https://, API_URL must be https:// too. The browser blocks an http:// API from an https:// page and the console shows a generic network error. See Web console.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: What Axium protects, how, and what is left to you.

docs.title: Secrets at rest
docs.text:
Secret Storage Mechanism Provider credentials (API keys, service-account JSON) llm.providers.api_key AES-256-GCM with MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY, random 12-byte IV per value, stored as base64(iv):base64(tag):base64(ciphertext). Decrypted on every proxied request. Never returned by the API; only the last 4 characters are exposed as api_key_masked. Console user passwords core.users bcrypt, 10 rounds. Minimum 8 characters. Console session tokens core.users.token 40 random hex characters (20 bytes from the system CSPRNG). Stored in clear, compared directly. Runtime API keys rm.api_keys.key_hash SHA-1 of the plaintext ax_… key, plus the last 4 characters. The plaintext is shown once, at creation, and cannot be recovered.

The master key cannot be rotated

There is no re-encryption procedure and no KMS integration. Losing or changing MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY means re-entering every provider's credentials by hand. Store it with the same care as the database backups, ideally in a secret manager, and never in the same place as the backup itself.

docs.title: Console sessions
docs.text:
• Login (POST /v1/users/login) returns a bearer token. It is not a JWT: it is an opaque value looked up in the database on every request.
  • Tokens do not expire. They are rotated (and the previous session invalidated) on each login, on logout, when the user is deactivated and when an administrator resets the password.
  • No cookies, no refresh tokens, no server-side session memory. Any replica can validate any token.

Because tokens never expire, encourage administrators to log out, and deactivate accounts of people who leave rather than just deleting their roles.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
Role-based. Permissions are module:action strings across eight modules (core, rm, llm, observability, governance, chat, mcp, agents) and nine actions (read, view, create, update, delete, manage, execute, test, export). Each route lists the permissions that open it and the caller needs at least one. The seeded super-admin role holds all 72 and cannot be removed from the last user who has it (409 LAST_SUPER_ADMIN).

There is no multi-tenancy: one installation is one tenant. Isolation between teams is done with proxy apps, API keys scoped to them, and model allow-lists.

docs.title: Runtime API keys
docs.text:
• Format ax_ followed by 40 hex characters.
  • Accepted as Authorization: Bearer ax_… or x-goog-api-key: ax_…. A ?key= query parameter is not accepted and is stripped before forwarding.
  • Scoped to one proxy app. Using a key against another app's URL answers 403. Unknown, inactive and expired keys answer an identical 401.
  • Optional expires_at. Deactivate (is_active=false) rather than delete to keep history.

Details in Authentication.

docs.title: What reaches the provider
docs.text:
Before forwarding, the core removes authorization, x-goog-api-key, api-key, x-api-key, cookie, host, hop-by-hop headers and the key query parameter, and injects the provider's own credential. No x-axium-* header is forwarded; they are consumed for tracing. The request body goes through as-is, except the model field (replaced by the deployed model name) and, in streamed chat completions, stream_options.include_usage=true.

Prompts and responses are not persisted by observability. The only place provider output is stored is the response cache (rm.request_io), and only when a proxy app enables the cache policy in strict mode.

docs.title: Data-loss prevention
docs.text: The dlp_prompt policy scans prompts for personal data (European identifiers, IBANs, phone numbers, …) and can mask values before they leave your network, block the request (403) or just record what it found. The trace records entity names and kinds, never the values. Configured per proxy app; see Proxy apps & gateways.

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
• TLS: terminate it in front of Axium, set TRUST_PROXY=true. See Reverse proxy & TLS.
  • CORS: the core answers Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * without credentials. This is not configurable. It is what lets the console run on another hostname; bearer tokens, not cookies, carry the identity, so the open origin does not enable cross-site request forgery.
  • Inbound firewall: the firewall.inbound policy restricts which client CIDRs may use a proxy app (first matching rule wins, up to 256 rules). It needs TRUST_PROXY=true behind a proxy to see real addresses; an unknown IP falls to default_action.
  • Egress: the core needs HTTPS to your providers and to meta.axium-lab.com. Nothing else.

docs.title: Lock these down at the ingress
docs.text: Route Why GET /v1/install/status, POST /v1/install Public by design so a fresh install can be driven without credentials. Inert once installed, but they reveal the schema version. Restrict to your admin network. GET /v1/health Harmless, but there is no reason for the internet to probe it. The console (ui) Behind SSO, a VPN or at least an IP allow-list if your team is small.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
• The container runs as the unprivileged bun user; nothing is written to disk.
  • Secrets arrive only through environment variables or a mounted license file. On Cloud Run the installer leaves them as plain environment variables; move them to Secret Manager for production.
  • There is no audit log of console actions in this version (the table exists in the schema but nothing writes to it). Observability traces cover runtime requests, not administrative changes.

docs.title: Web console (ui)
docs.text: The ui is a static web application served by a small Node server on port 3001. It has one configuration variable.

docs.title: API_URL
docs.text:
docker run -d --name axium-ui -p 3001:3001 \
  -e API_URL=https://axium-api.your-domain.com/v1 \
  quay.io/axiumlab/ui:latest

The URL of the core's API as seen from the user's browser. The ui injects it into the page; the browser then calls it directly. The ui container itself never talks to the core.

Rules:

  • It must be reachable from wherever the users are: a public hostname, a VPN address, http://localhost:3000/v1 on a laptop.
  • It must end in /v1 with no trailing slash.
  • An internal Docker or Kubernetes name (http://axium-core:3000/v1) does not work, even though the ui container can resolve it. The browser cannot.
  • If the ui is served over https://, API_URL must be https:// too. Otherwise the browser blocks the requests as mixed content and the login page shows only a network error.

docs.title: Same host or different hosts?
docs.text: Both work. The core answers CORS pre-flights for any origin, so the console can live on axium.your-domain.com while the API lives on axium-api.your-domain.com. If you prefer a single hostname, route /v1/* to the core and everything else to the ui at the proxy.

docs.title: Health
docs.text: The ui has no status endpoint. A 200 on / is all there is to check; the Google Cloud updater does exactly that.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: The ui consumes the core's API, so upgrade the core first, then the ui. The ui is stateless: stop it, remove it, start the new tag.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Axium ships as two container images plus a PostgreSQL database. This section takes you from nothing to a working installation you can log in to.

  • Requirements

    What you need before you start: Docker, a PostgreSQL 17 database, a Quay token and your Axium license.

    Requirements

  • Install with Docker

    Three docker run commands. The fastest way to evaluate Axium on a laptop or a single VM.

    Docker

  • Install with Docker Compose

    The same deployment as a single, versionable compose.yaml.

    Docker Compose

  • Install on Google Cloud

    One script creates Cloud SQL, copies the images and deploys both services to Cloud Run.

    Google Cloud

docs.title: The three pieces
docs.text:
Piece Image What it is State core quay.io/axiumlab/core The API: authentication, provider gateways, observability. Listens on port 3000. Stateless ui quay.io/axiumlab/ui The web console. A static site served by Node on port 3001. Stateless PostgreSQL postgres:17-alpine or a managed service Everything Axium persists. The only state

The core and the ui never write to disk. The PostgreSQL volume is the only thing you have to back up.

docs.title: Image tags
docs.text:
Both images publish the same three tags:

Tag Meaning Use it for vX.Y.Z (e.g. v0.1.0) A specific, immutable version. Production. vX-latest (e.g. v1-latest) The latest release of that major. Staging. latest The latest release published. Evaluation. 
docker login quay.io
docker pull quay.io/axiumlab/core:latest
docker pull quay.io/axiumlab/ui:latest

docs.title: Install with Docker Compose
docs.text: The same deployment as the Docker guide, expressed as one file you can keep in version control.

docs.title: compose.yaml
docs.text:
compose.yaml
name: axium

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: axium
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set it in .env}
      POSTGRES_DB: axium-api
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U axium -d axium-api"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 12

  core:
    image: quay.io/axiumlab/core:${AXIUM_TAG:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://axium:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/axium-api
      MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY:?generate it with: openssl rand -hex 32}
      AXIUM_LICENSE: ${AXIUM_LICENSE:-}
      # Only when a reverse proxy terminates TLS in front of the core:
      # TRUST_PROXY: "true"
      # PUBLIC_BASE_URL: https://axium-api.your-domain.com
    healthcheck:
      # The image has no curl or wget; bun is the available HTTP client.
      test: ["CMD", "bun", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/v1/install/status').then(r => r.json()).then(j => process.exit(j.data.state === 'installed' ? 0 : 1)).catch(() => process.exit(1))"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      start_period: 60s
      retries: 5

  ui:
    image: quay.io/axiumlab/ui:${AXIUM_TAG:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - core
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    environment:
      # Resolved by the browser, not by this container. Must be reachable from
      # the outside and end in /v1 with no trailing slash.
      API_URL: ${API_URL:-http://localhost:3000/v1}

volumes:
  pgdata:

Health checks

The core image already declares a liveness HEALTHCHECK on /v1/health. The one above replaces it with a readiness check on the schema state. See Health checks.

docs.title: .env
docs.text:
.env
AXIUM_TAG=v0.1.0
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-this
MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY=   # openssl rand -hex 32
AXIUM_LICENSE=           # your 40-character hex license
API_URL=http://localhost:3000/v1

Keep .env out of version control: it holds the master key and the database password.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
docker login quay.io
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
curl http://localhost:3000/v1/install/status

Then open http://localhost:3001 and continue with First login.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
Change AXIUM_TAG in .env and run:

docker compose pull && docker compose up -d

The containers are disposable and the pgdata volume stays where it is. Read Upgrading before moving across a major version.

docs.title: Install with Docker
docs.text:
This is the minimum needed to bring Axium up with plain docker run and log in for the first time. It is the right choice for an evaluation or a single VM. For anything you intend to keep, prefer Docker Compose so the configuration lives in a file.

Installing on Google Cloud?

Do not follow this guide. Use the Google Cloud installer, which creates Cloud SQL, deploys both services to Cloud Run and verifies the installation for you.

docs.title: 1. Log in to the registry
docs.text:
The images are private. One Quay token works for both core and ui:

docker login quay.io

docs.title: 2. Create a network
docs.text:
The core needs to reach PostgreSQL by name:

docker network create axium

docs.title: 3. Start PostgreSQL
docs.text:
docker run -d --name axium-db --network axium \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -e POSTGRES_USER=axium \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-this \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=axium-api \
  -v axium-pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  postgres:17-alpine

The axium-pgdata volume is the only state you have to preserve. See Backup & restore.

docs.title: 4. Generate the master key
docs.text:
The core encrypts the provider credentials it stores in the database with a master key. Generate it once and store it in your password manager:

openssl rand -hex 32

The master key cannot be rotated

If MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY is lost or changed, none of the stored provider credentials can be decrypted and all of them have to be entered again by hand. Treat it like a database backup: without it the backup is incomplete.

docs.title: 5. Start the core
docs.text:
docker run -d --name axium-core --network axium \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  -e DATABASE_URL=postgresql://axium:change-this@axium-db:5432/axium-api \
  -e MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<the 64 hex characters from the previous step> \
  -e AXIUM_LICENSE=<your 40-character license> \
  quay.io/axiumlab/core:latest

DATABASE_URL and MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY are the only mandatory variables. Without either of them, or with a key that is not exactly 64 hexadecimal characters, the process refuses to start. Everything else is optional and documented in Environment variables.

On the first startup the core waits for PostgreSQL (up to 30 seconds), installs the schema itself and creates the initial user. Restarting it repeats nothing.

docs.title: 6. Start the ui
docs.text:
docker run -d --name axium-ui --network axium \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 3001:3001 \
  -e API_URL=http://localhost:3000/v1 \
  quay.io/axiumlab/ui:latest

API_URL is the ui's only variable and it is resolved by the user's browser, not by the container. It has to be the URL the core is reached at from the outside. In a real deployment that is something like https://axium-api.your-domain.com/v1. An internal Docker name such as http://axium-core:3000/v1 does not work, even though the ui container can resolve it. It must end in /v1 with no trailing slash. See Web console.

docs.title: 7. Check that it is up
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:3000/v1/health          # {"status":"ok"}
curl http://localhost:3000/v1/install/status  # {"state":"installed", ...}

You need both. /v1/health answers ok even if the schema installation failed, so the one that confirms Axium is usable is /v1/install/status. If it returns anything other than installed, check the logs:

docker logs axium-core | grep '\[install\]'

The full list of states is in Health checks.

docs.title: 8. Log in
docs.text: Open http://localhost:3001 and continue with First login.

docs.title: First login
docs.text:
Open the web console (http://localhost:3001 in the Docker guides, the Cloud Run URL on Google Cloud) and log in with the credentials the schema creates:

User admin@axium.local Password admin123456

They are the same in every new installation and have full permissions.

Change them as soon as you log in

There is no way to set different initial credentials from the configuration: every fresh installation starts with this account. Change the password immediately, and create personal accounts for the people who will administer the installation.

docs.title: What to do next
docs.text:
1. Change the admin password.
  2. Store the master key (MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY) in your password manager if you have not already. It cannot be rotated and cannot be recovered from the database.
  3. Add a provider. Provider credentials (OpenAI, Google, …) are entered in the console and stored encrypted in PostgreSQL. See Security.
  4. Create a proxy app and an API key, then point an SDK at it. See Proxy apps & gateways and SDK examples.
  5. Configure an observability destination so every request is recorded where you want it. See Observability.

docs.title: Install on Google Cloud
docs.text: infra-gcp/gcp.sh installs Axium in a Google Cloud project from Cloud Shell: a Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL 17) instance, and the core and the ui as two Cloud Run services. It is meant to be pasted and waited on, and it is idempotent: you can re-run it to upgrade versions without losing the database or the master key.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
Open Cloud Shell in the target project and run:

wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/axium-lab/infrastructure-documentation/refs/heads/main/infra-gcp/gcp.sh \
  && chmod +x gcp.sh \
  && TAG=v0.1.0 ./gcp.sh

The script asks for two things it cannot find on its own:

  • Your Axium license (40 hexadecimal characters). It is checked against the Axium Lab license API before anything is created, so a mistyped or expired license fails in seconds rather than after ten minutes of Cloud SQL provisioning. If the license API cannot be reached the script warns and continues: the core validates the license again at startup.
  • Your Quay user and token, unless a session already exists.

Plan for 10 to 15 minutes, most of it waiting for Cloud SQL.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
All options are environment variables:

Variable Default Effect TAG latest Image tag to deploy. Pin a version in production: TAG=v0.1.0. REGION europe-west1 Region for Cloud SQL, Artifact Registry and Cloud Run. PROJECT_ID current gcloud project Target project. AXIUM_LICENSE asked interactively License key. Pass it in pipelines; an invalid value aborts instead of prompting. VERTEX_PROJECT PROJECT_ID Project where Vertex AI lives, if different. The IAM role is granted there. DB_INSTANCE / DB_NAME / DB_USER axium-db / axium-api / axium Cloud SQL names. AR_REPO axium Artifact Registry repository. CORE_SERVICE / UI_SERVICE axium-core / axium-ui Cloud Run service names. DEBUG unset 1 prints registry connectivity diagnostics and runs crane in verbose mode. AXIUM_NO_CRANE unset 1 forces the Docker daemon for image copies instead of crane.

docs.title: What it creates
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    B[Browser] -->|HTTPS| UI[Cloud Run<br/>axium-ui]
    B -->|HTTPS · API_URL| CORE[Cloud Run<br/>axium-core]
    CORE -->|Unix socket /cloudsql| SQL[(Cloud SQL<br/>PostgreSQL 17)]
    CORE -->|OAuth2 · roles/aiplatform.user| VX[Vertex AI]
    CORE -->|roles/storage.objectUser| GCS[(Cloud Storage)]
    Q[quay.io/axiumlab] -->|crane copy| AR[Artifact Registry<br/>REGION-docker.pkg.dev]
    AR --> UI
    AR --> CORE

Step by step:

  1. License check against https://meta.axium-lab.com/v1/license/check/<license>.
  2. APIs: sqladmin, run, artifactregistry, storage in the project, and aiplatform in VERTEX_PROJECT (a failure there only warns).
  3. Artifact Registry repository axium. Cloud Run can only deploy from Artifact Registry, so the images are copied from Quay with crane (falls back to the Docker daemon). Downloads of crane are cached in ~/.axium/bin.
  4. Cloud SQL: the cheapest configuration that exists, intended for a pilot. db-f1-micro, 10 GB HDD, single zone, no automatic backups. For production remove --no-backup and pick a bigger tier.
  5. Secrets: MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY and DATABASE_URL are read back from the deployed core if it exists and generated otherwise. The master key is never regenerated once it exists. The DSN uses the Cloud SQL Unix socket: postgresql://axium:<pass>@localhost/axium-api?host=/cloudsql/<connectionName>.

  6. IAM on the runtime service account (the project's default compute SA unless the service already uses another):

    Role Project Why roles/cloudsql.client deploy Connect through the /cloudsql socket. roles/storage.objectUser deploy Read, write and delete objects in buckets. roles/storage.bucketViewer deploy List buckets and read metadata; objectUser alone makes bucket.exists() return 403. roles/aiplatform.user VERTEX_PROJECT Call Google models through Vertex AI. Publisher models do not accept per-resource IAM, so the binding is project-wide.

  7. Core on Cloud Run: --allow-unauthenticated, 1 GiB RAM, 1 vCPU, concurrency 20, 0 to 4 instances, with DATABASE_URL, MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY, TRUST_PROXY=true and AXIUM_LICENSE. Memory and concurrency follow from the 50 MB upload ceiling, which is held in RAM per request.

  8. Ui on Cloud Run: 512 MiB, concurrency 80, API_URL=<core URL>/v1.
  9. Verification: waits for /v1/health, then requires /v1/install/status to answer installed.

The script ends with the console URL, the API URL, the initial credentials and the master key in clear text. Save it before closing the shell.

docs.title: After installing
docs.text:
• Change the admin password (First login).
  • Move the secrets to Secret Manager. The master key and the database password are in clear text in the Cloud Run service configuration, visible to anyone with read access to the project. Replace --set-env-vars with --set-secrets in the script to harden it.

  • Renewing the license does not require reinstalling:

    gcloud run services update axium-core --region europe-west1 \
  --update-env-vars AXIUM_LICENSE=<the new one>

  • Vertex AI in another project. The core calls Vertex with the project_id configured in the provider inside Axium. If that is not the deploy project, re-run with VERTEX_PROJECT=<that project> bash gcp.sh or grant roles/aiplatform.user there by hand, otherwise generation fails with 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.

  • Public services. If the deploy fails mentioning IAM or allUsers, your organization's domain-restricted-sharing policy forbids public Cloud Run services. Deploy with --no-allow-unauthenticated and put a load balancer or IAP in front.

docs.title: Several environments in one project
docs.text:
infra-gcp/gcp-environments.sh is the same installer with an environment prefix. It asks for a name (dev, test, pre, …) and creates <env>-axium-core, <env>-axium-ui and a database <env>-axium-api inside the same Cloud SQL instance, which is the only piece that costs money to duplicate.

AXIUM_ENV=dev TAG=v0.1.0 bash gcp-environments.sh   # non-interactive
AXIUM_ENV= bash gcp-environments.sh                 # empty = no prefix, same as gcp.sh

Each environment gets its own master key and its own database user password, read back from its own Cloud Run service on re-runs.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: Use infra-gcp/update.sh. It is covered in Upgrading.

docs.title: Cost notes
docs.text: With the defaults, idle cost is dominated by the Cloud SQL instance (db-f1-micro, always on). Both Cloud Run services scale to zero. The first request after a scale-to-zero pays a cold start of a few seconds; on the core that cold start also runs the schema check.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
Requirement Notes Container runtime Docker 24+ or any OCI runtime (Kubernetes, Cloud Run, ECS, …) Images are multi-arch: linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. PostgreSQL 17 recommended (the version used in development and CI). Technical minimum 13. No extensions required. See Database. Registry access A Quay token for quay.io/axiumlab One token works for core and ui. License Your Axium license key (40 hexadecimal characters) See License. Outbound network HTTPS to your LLM providers, and to meta.axium-lab.com for license checks and telemetry Telemetry can be disabled; see Environment variables. TLS termination A reverse proxy or load balancer in front of the core and the ui Axium does not terminate TLS. See Reverse proxy & TLS.

Nothing else: no Node.js, no Redis, no object storage, no message queue. The core image embeds its own runtime (Bun) and runs as a non-root user.

docs.title: Sizing
docs.text:
The core is stateless and light. What drives memory is request size, not request count:

  • Every file upload is held entirely in RAM for the duration of the request, up to MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE (default 50 MB).
  • Every streamed response is kept in memory until it finishes, so usage and cost can be read at the end.
  • The observability buffer holds up to 10,000 traces per process.
  • JSON bodies are capped at 10 MB.

Starting points that work:

Workload Core Ui PostgreSQL Evaluation, a handful of developers 512 MiB · 0.5 vCPU 256 MiB smallest tier (the GCP installer uses db-f1-micro, 10 GB) Production, chat traffic 1 GiB · 1 vCPU per replica, concurrency ≈ 20 512 MiB 2 vCPU · 4 GB · SSD, automated backups Production with large uploads 2 GiB+ per replica, or lower MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE 512 MiB as above

Scale the core horizontally rather than vertically; see Scaling & sizing.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Component Port Protocol core 3000 (configurable with PORT) HTTP. Everything is under /v1/. ui 3001 HTTP. Static files. PostgreSQL 5432 Reached only by the core.

docs.title: Database permissions
docs.text: The core installs and migrates its own schema. The database user needs to be able to CREATE SCHEMA and create tables, types, functions and triggers in the database. It creates the schemas core, llm, rm and stats, plus telemetry if the PostgreSQL observability destination is enabled.

docs.title: Time zone
docs.text: Daily statistics and budget windows are computed with the PostgreSQL server's time zone (CURRENT_DATE, date_trunc(..., now())). Set the database to the time zone you want your "days" and "months" to follow, typically UTC.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
Axium records what happens to every request that goes through a proxy app, at two levels:

  • Daily statistics · always on

    Aggregates per proxy app, day, model and API key in the main database (stats.proxy_daily): requests, tokens and cost. They power the console's dashboards and GET /v1/stats/proxy.

  • Per-request traces · opt-in

    One record per request with identity, model, tokens, cost, timing, result, policies and client tags. Sent to the destination you choose: PostgreSQL or an HTTP endpoint.

    Destinations

Plus plain-text process logs on stdout, described in Request logging.

docs.title: Turning traces on
docs.text:
Traces are off by default. One variable selects the destination, the rest configure it. Configuration is global to the installation and lives only in environment variables; there is no per-app, console or API switch.

PostgreSQLHTTP (envelope)HTTP (NDJSON) 
OBSERVABILITY_TYPE=postgres
OBSERVABILITY_DB_POSTGRESQL=postgresql://axium:secret@db:5432/axium-api

Writes to telemetry.proxy_traces and makes traces queryable through GET /v1/observability/traces. Details

OBSERVABILITY_TYPE=http
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_URL=https://collector.example.com/axium
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_HEADERS='{"Authorization":"Bearer xxx"}'

POSTs {"version":1,"data":[…]} batches. Details

OBSERVABILITY_TYPE=http
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_URL=https://clickhouse.example.com/?query=INSERT%20INTO%20axium.traces%20FORMAT%20JSONEachRow
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_FORMAT=ndjson
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_HEADERS='{"X-ClickHouse-Key":"xxx"}'

One JSON object per line, ready for ClickHouse JSONEachRow, BigQuery loads, Vector, Fluent Bit or a Lambda. Details

At startup the log confirms the result:

[observability] enabled (postgres)
[observability] enabled (http, ndjson)
[observability] disabled: <reason>

GET /v1/diagnostics (authenticated) reports the same under observability.

docs.title: What a trace contains
docs.text:
Metadata only, never content:

Recorded Not recorded Proxy app, API key, client IP, client user id and tags you send Prompts and responses, even truncated Provider, region, model requested and model used, surface, upstream path Client headers other than x-axium-* Tokens (in, out, cached, reasoning), cost in and out Credentials of any kind Timing, streaming flag, max tokens Status, HTTP status, error origin, category and provider message Policies applied, denial reason, DLP findings (entity kinds, not values)

The exact schema, with types and the values each field can take, is in Formats & event schema.

docs.title: How delivery works
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as Request
    participant B as In-memory buffer<br/>(per core process)
    participant D as Destination
    R->>B: add(trace) · synchronous, never throws
    Note over B: flush every 2 s, or as soon as 50 traces are queued
    B->>D: batch of ≤ 50 traces
    alt write fails
        Note over B: batch dropped, counted as lost,<br/>logged at most once per 5 min
    end
    Note over B: cap 10,000 traces · oldest dropped beyond that
  • Recording never slows down or fails a request.
  • Batches are not retried. A destination outage loses the batches sent during it; the log says how many: [observability] write failed, N trace(s) lost so far: <error>.
  • On SIGTERM the buffer is flushed in one attempt per batch before exit.
  • The buffer is per process. A replica that is killed loses up to 2 seconds of traces, or more if the destination was slow.

If you need at-least-once delivery, point the HTTP destination at a local collector (Vector, Fluent Bit, an OTel Collector with an HTTP receiver) that queues on disk and forwards.

docs.title: Destinations
docs.text:
Exactly two destinations exist. Pick with OBSERVABILITY_TYPE.

postgres http Where traces go A PostgreSQL table, telemetry.proxy_traces Any HTTP endpoint, one POST per batch Readable through Axium's API Yes, GET /v1/observability/traces No (409 on that route) Schema managed by Axium Yes, created and migrated at startup No, the receiver owns it Formats Table rows envelope (JSON) or ndjson Computed fields (latency_ms, tokens_total, cost) Generated columns You compute them Authentication to the destination In the DSN OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_HEADERS Timeout per write 10 s to acquire a connection 5 s per request Good for Getting started, small and medium volumes, querying from the console or SQL Feeding ClickHouse, BigQuery, Datadog, Splunk, S3, a SIEM, or a collector

Common behaviour (batching, drops, no retries) is described in the overview. Delivery details for each:

  • PostgreSQL destination
  • HTTP destination

docs.title: Not available
docs.text: There is no console, file, OpenTelemetry/OTLP, Langfuse, OpenInference or vendor-native exporter in this version. All of those are reachable through the HTTP destination with a collector in between: an OpenTelemetry Collector or Vector can receive the NDJSON stream over HTTP and fan it out.

docs.title: Choosing
docs.text:
• Start with postgres on the same database. It costs nothing extra, the console can show traces, and telemetry.proxy_traces is a normal table you can query, export or replicate.
  • Move to http when you want traces in the same place as the rest of your telemetry, when volume grows beyond what you want in the transactional database, or when you need durable delivery through a collector.
  • You cannot run both at once. To get both, use http into a collector that writes to PostgreSQL and elsewhere.

docs.title: Formats & event schema
docs.text:
A trace is the record Axium emits for every request that reaches a proxy app runtime: successful, failed, denied by a policy or served from cache. This page is the contract for anyone consuming traces, whether from the PostgreSQL table or from an HTTP batch.

Schema version 1 (header x-axium-trace-version on HTTP; telemetry.schema_version in PostgreSQL) Cardinality Exactly one trace per request Fields emitted 42, always present, always in the order below Computed in PostgreSQL only latency_ms, tokens_total, cost Unknown values null. Token counts are never defaulted to 0. Timestamps ISO-8601 in UTC with milliseconds (2026-10-19T10:15:30.120Z)

docs.title: Identity
docs.text: Field Type Description trace_id uuid Minted when the request enters Axium and returned to the client in the x-axium-trace-id response header. Lets a client report "this request" and you find it. span_id uuid One span per trace in this version.

docs.title: Timing
docs.text: Field Type Description started_at timestamp When the request entered Axium. ended_at timestamp When the response finished. For streams, when the last chunk was sent. latency_ms integer · computed ended_at - started_at.

docs.title: Origin
docs.text: Field Type Description source_module proxy Reserved for other modules in future versions. proxy_app_id uuid · null The proxy app in the URL. null only when the app does not exist. api_key_id uuid · null The key that authenticated. client_ip string · null req.ip. The real client only with TRUST_PROXY=true behind a proxy. Personal data. client_country null Reserved. No geolocation in this version. client_user_id string · null Value of the x-axium-user-id request header, if the client sent one.

docs.title: Provider and model
docs.text:
Field Type Description provider_id uuid · null provider_type openai · azure-openai · google-aistudio · google-enterprise · null provider_region string · null Provider's configured region, global by default. model_id uuid · null Axium's model record. model_used string · null Deployed model name sent upstream. On Vertex includes the publisher: google/gemini-2.5-flash, anthropic/claude-…. model_requested string · null What the client asked for. null when the app's default model was used. dialect openai · gemini Wire protocol of the gateway. surface see below Which endpoint family was called. upstream_path string · null Path sent to the provider, e.g. /v1/chat/completions. null if the request never left Axium (denied, cache hit).

surface values: openai.chat, openai.responses, openai.models, openai.files, gemini.generate, gemini.interactions, gemini.models, gemini.files, vertex.generate.

docs.title: Tokens
docs.text:
All integer · null. null means the provider did not report it.

Field Source tokens_in Prompt tokens. tokens_out Completion tokens. tokens_cache_read Prompt tokens served from the provider's cache (cached_tokens). tokens_cache_write Reserved, always null. tokens_reasoning Reasoning tokens (reasoning_tokens). tokens_saved Reserved, always null. tokens_total computed: tokens_in + tokens_out.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
All number · null, six decimals, in the currency of the prices configured on the model. null when the model has no price.

Field Definition cost_in tokens_in × cost_input_1m / 1e6. Cached tokens are billed at full input price. cost_out tokens_out × cost_output_1m / 1e6. cost_saved Reserved, always null. cost computed: cost_in + cost_out.

docs.title: Request shape
docs.text: Field Type Description stream boolean Whether the client asked for streaming. max_tokens integer · null max_completion_tokens or max_tokens (chat), max_output_tokens (responses), generationConfig.maxOutputTokens (Gemini/Vertex).

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Field Type Description status success · error · denied · timeout · cancelled denied = Axium refused before calling the provider. cancelled = the client closed a stream early. http_status integer What the client received. error_origin axium · provider · null Who produced the error. error_category see below · null Normalised category. error_message string · null The provider's error.message, or Axium's own message. cache_hit boolean · null true/false only when the cache policy ran; null otherwise. fallback_used null Reserved.

error_category values: auth_error, permission_denied, not_found, rate_limit, quota_exceeded, content_filter, invalid_request, server_error, timeout, connection_error, unknown. For non-streamed provider errors it is derived from the status: 401 → auth_error, 403 → permission_denied, 404 → not_found, 429 → rate_limit, 5xx → server_error, other 4xx → invalid_request.

docs.title: Policies
docs.text: Field Type Description policies_applied string[] Policies that ran, whether or not they changed anything: firewall.inbound, dlp_prompt, cache. denial_reason string · null Only with status = denied. See the table below. denial_reason HTTP Meaning app_not_found 404 No proxy app with that id. app_not_ready 403 App is draft or inactive. budget_exhausted 429 The app's budget for the current period is spent. model_ambiguous 400 The name matches more than one allowed model. model_not_allowed 403 Model is not in the app's allow-list. no_default_model 400 Client sent no model and the app has no default. default_model_unusable 403 The default model is inactive or not allowed. provider_inactive 403 The model's provider is deactivated. provider_type_mismatch 400 E.g. an OpenAI model through the Gemini gateway. dialect_mismatch 400 The model's provider does not speak this gateway's protocol. streaming_unsupported 400 Streaming requested on a surface that does not support it. firewall_denied 403 Client IP blocked by firewall.inbound. dlp_blocked 403 dlp_prompt found data the policy blocks. policy_config_invalid 500 The app's policy document could not be applied.

docs.title: Context
Sending context from your application
docs.text:
Three request headers feed the trace and are never forwarded to the provider:

x-axium-user-id: user-42            → client_user_id
x-axium-meta-tag: release-2026.10   → meta_tag
x-axium-team: sales                 → tags.team
x-axium-feature: summarise          → tags.feature

Most SDKs accept default headers:

new OpenAI({ apiKey, baseURL, defaultHeaders: { 'x-axium-user-id': user.id, 'x-axium-team': 'sales' } });

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: The schema version increments when a field changes meaning or is removed. Adding a field does not bump it. Consumers should ignore unknown fields and check x-axium-trace-version (HTTP) or telemetry.schema_version (PostgreSQL).

docs.title: HTTP destination
docs.text:
OBSERVABILITY_TYPE=http
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_URL=https://collector.example.com/axium/traces
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_FORMAT=envelope          # or ndjson
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_HEADERS='{"Authorization":"Bearer xxx"}'

The core POSTs each batch (up to 50 traces, at most 2 s apart) to the URL. Nothing is read back: the destination is write-only, and GET /v1/observability/traces answers 409 under this destination.

docs.title: The request
docs.text:
Method POST Timeout 5 s per request (connection + response) Retries None. A failed batch is dropped and counted. Success Any 2xx. Anything else is logged with the first 200 bytes of the body: [observability] <url> answered 503 Service Unavailable <body> Headers set by Axium content-type: application/json (envelope) or application/x-ndjson (ndjson) · x-axium-trace-version: 1 Your headers OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_HEADERS, applied after Axium's, so they can override them

Errors are logged at most once every 5 minutes with a running count of lost traces. The URL is not probed at startup; a typo surfaces on the first flush.

docs.title: Formats
ClickHouse
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE axium.traces (

  started_at DateTime64(3, 'UTC'), ended_at DateTime64(3, 'UTC'),

  client_ip Nullable(String), client_country Nullable(String), client_user_id Nullable(String),

  model_id Nullable(UUID), model_used Nullable(String), model_requested Nullable(String),
  dialect LowCardinality(Nullable(String)), surface LowCardinality(Nullable(String)), upstream_path Nullable(String),
  tokens_in Nullable(Int32), tokens_out Nullable(Int32), tokens_cache_read Nullable(Int32),
  tokens_cache_write Nullable(Int32), tokens_reasoning Nullable(Int32), tokens_saved Nullable(Int32),
  cost_in Nullable(Decimal(14,6)), cost_out Nullable(Decimal(14,6)), cost_saved Nullable(Decimal(14,6)),
  stream Nullable(Bool), max_tokens Nullable(Int32),
