docs.title: Vector (to anywhere)
docs.text:
vector.toml
[sources.axium]
type = "http_server"
address = "0.0.0.0:8686"
decoding.codec = "json"            # one event per NDJSON line
path = "/axium"

[sinks.s3]
type = "aws_s3"
inputs = ["axium"]
bucket = "llm-traces"
key_prefix = "axium/date=%Y-%m-%d/"
encoding.codec = "json"
buffer.type = "disk"               # durable: survives a slow S3
buffer.max_size = 268435488

OBSERVABILITY_TYPE=http
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_FORMAT=ndjson
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_URL=http://vector:8686/axium

A local collector with a disk buffer is the recommended way to get at-least-once delivery, since Axium itself does not retry.

docs.title: Datadog Logs
docs.text:
OBSERVABILITY_TYPE=http
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_FORMAT=envelope
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_URL=https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.eu/api/v2/logs?ddsource=axium&service=axium
OBSERVABILITY_HTTP_HEADERS='{"DD-API-KEY":"…"}'

Datadog's intake accepts a JSON array, so send the envelope through a small transform (a Datadog pipeline or a Lambda) that unwraps data, or use the NDJSON format through the Datadog Agent's HTTP log listener.

docs.title: A webhook of your own
docs.text:
// Node/Express receiver, envelope format
app.post('/axium', express.json({ limit: '2mb' }), (req, res) => {
  if (req.get('x-axium-trace-version') !== '1') return res.status(400).end();
  for (const trace of req.body.data) store(trace);
  res.sendStatus(204);               // any 2xx acknowledges the batch
});

Answer quickly: the core waits at most 5 s and does not retry. Accept, queue, process later.

docs.title: Request logging
docs.text: Besides traces, the core writes plain-text logs to stdout and stderr. There is no log level, no JSON mode and no file output; collect the container's streams with your usual tooling.

docs.title: Log prefixes
docs.text: Prefix What it reports [server] Listening port and environment; shutdown progress. [db] Connection wait and success; pool closed on shutdown. [install] Schema installation, migration and their failures. Read these first when /v1/install/status is not installed. [license] Result of the license check at startup. [telemetry] Whether the anonymous snapshot was sent. [observability] Destination enabled or disabled, lost batches (throttled to one line per 5 minutes), shutdown flush. [req] One line per HTTP request, only with LOG_REQUESTS=true. [runtime] One line per request forwarded to a provider: [runtime] <surface> <METHOD> <path> <model>, plus warnings such as could not record usage, stream ended early, dlp could not run. [usage] Token usage returned by the provider on non-streamed calls: [usage] <model> <surface> {…}. [errorHandler] Unexpected 500s with the real cause. The client only sees INTERNAL_ERROR. [proxy-runtime] Unexpected errors inside the gateway.

docs.title: Per-request lines
docs.text:
LOG_REQUESTS=true

[req] POST /v1/proxy-apps/9a1b…/openai/v1/chat/completions 200 843ms
[req] GET /v1/users/me 200 4ms
[req] POST /v1/proxy-apps/9a1b…/openai/v1/responses 200 15210ms (aborted)

(aborted) marks a client that closed the connection before the response was complete. The middleware runs before the body parser, so malformed JSON requests are logged as well. Off by default in production because, at volume, traces are the better record: they carry tokens, cost and identity, and go to a database rather than a log stream.

docs.title: A typical startup
docs.text:
[license] valid — Acme Corp (enterprise), expires 2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
[db] waiting for postgres...
[db] connected
[install] schema version 3 is current
[observability] schema version 1 is current
[observability] enabled (postgres)
[server] listening on port 3000 (production)
[telemetry] anonymous snapshot sent — disable with TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false

docs.title: A typical shutdown
docs.text:
[server] SIGTERM received, closing
[db] pool closed

Shutdown waits for in-flight requests (long streams delay it) up to 10 s, then logs [server] shutdown timed out, forcing exit and exits with code 1. Give the container at least 15 s of grace.

docs.title: Shipping logs
docs.text: Nothing special: docker logs, gcloud run services logs read, a Kubernetes log agent. For Cloud Run, the [req] and [runtime] lines are parsed as text entries in Cloud Logging; filter with textPayload:"[install]".

docs.title: PostgreSQL destination
docs.text:
OBSERVABILITY_TYPE=postgres
OBSERVABILITY_DB_POSTGRESQL=postgresql://axium:secret@db:5432/axium-api

The DSN can point at the main Axium database or at a separate one on any PostgreSQL 13+ server. The core opens its own pool for it (max 8 connections, 10 s to acquire one) so trace writes never compete with the request path for connections.

docs.title: Schema management
docs.text:
At every start the core checks the telemetry schema in the trace database with the same logic it uses for its own schema:

Found Action Log Nothing Creates the schema, tables and indexes in one transaction [observability] schema version 1 installed Current version Nothing [observability] schema version 1 is current Older version Applies bundled migrations [observability] schema migrated a -> b telemetry schema without a version table Refuses; observability stays disabled for this process [observability] disabled: …

Several replicas can start at once; an advisory lock serialises the install. The user in the DSN needs CREATE on the database the first time.

docs.title: telemetry.proxy_traces
docs.text:
One row per request. Columns match the event schema one to one, plus three generated columns:

Column Definition latency_ms (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM ended_at - started_at) * 1000)::INTEGER tokens_total tokens_in + tokens_out (NULL if either is NULL) cost cost_in + cost_out (NULL if either is NULL)

Indexes:

Index Columns Purpose idx_telemetry_proxy_traces_app (proxy_app_id, provider_type, model_used, started_at) Per-app dashboards idx_telemetry_proxy_traces_started_at (started_at) Time ranges, retention jobs idx_telemetry_proxy_traces_trace_id (trace_id) WHERE trace_id IS NOT NULL Lookup by the x-axium-trace-id a client reports idx_telemetry_proxy_traces_tags GIN on tags Filter by client tags (tags @> '{"team":"sales"}') Full DDL 
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS telemetry;

CREATE TABLE telemetry.schema_version (
    version    INTEGER     NOT NULL,
    applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    install_id UUID        NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

);
INSERT INTO telemetry.schema_version (version) VALUES (1);

CREATE TABLE telemetry.schema_migrations (
    version    INTEGER     PRIMARY KEY,
    applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS telemetry.proxy_traces (
    trace_id            UUID,
    span_id             UUID,
    started_at          TIMESTAMPTZ,
    ended_at            TIMESTAMPTZ,
    latency_ms          INTEGER GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (ended_at - started_at)) * 1000)::INTEGER) STORED,
    source_module       TEXT,
    proxy_app_id        UUID,
    api_key_id          UUID,
    client_ip           INET,
    client_country      TEXT,
    client_user_id      TEXT,
    provider_id         UUID,
    provider_type       TEXT,
    provider_region     TEXT,
    model_id            UUID,
    model_used          TEXT,
    model_requested     TEXT,
    dialect             TEXT,
    surface             TEXT,
    upstream_path       TEXT,
    tokens_in           INTEGER,
    tokens_out          INTEGER,
    tokens_cache_read   INTEGER,
    tokens_cache_write  INTEGER,
    tokens_reasoning    INTEGER,
    tokens_saved        INTEGER,
    tokens_total        INTEGER GENERATED ALWAYS AS (tokens_in + tokens_out) STORED,
    cost_in             DECIMAL(14,6),
    cost_out            DECIMAL(14,6),
    cost                DECIMAL(14,6) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (cost_in + cost_out) STORED,
    cost_saved          DECIMAL(14,6),
    stream              BOOLEAN,
    max_tokens          INTEGER,
    error_origin        TEXT,
    status              TEXT,
    http_status         SMALLINT,
    error_category      TEXT,
    error_message       TEXT,
    cache_hit           BOOLEAN,
    fallback_used       BOOLEAN,
    policies_applied    TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    denial_reason       TEXT,
    meta_tag            TEXT,
    tags                JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    attributes          JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_telemetry_proxy_traces_app        ON telemetry.proxy_traces (proxy_app_id, provider_type, model_used, started_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_telemetry_proxy_traces_started_at ON telemetry.proxy_traces (started_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_telemetry_proxy_traces_trace_id   ON telemetry.proxy_traces (trace_id) WHERE trace_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_telemetry_proxy_traces_tags       ON telemetry.proxy_traces USING GIN (tags);

docs.title: Writes
docs.text: Each batch (up to 50 traces, at most 2 s apart) becomes one multi-row INSERT. A failed insert drops the batch; see delivery.

docs.title: Reading traces through the API
docs.text:
GET /v1/observability/traces (permission observability:read) queries the table. It exists only with this destination; with http or with observability off it answers 409 CONFLICT.

Query parameter Type Notes trace_id uuid Exact match. proxy_app_id uuid status success · error · denied · timeout · cancelled from, to ISO-8601 with offset (2026-01-01T00:00:00Z) Inclusive on started_at; from ≤ to. limit integer 1 to 1000 Default 100. Above 1000 is a 400, not clipped.

Rows come back newest first with the generated columns included:

{ "status": true, "data": [ { "trace_id": "…", "latency_ms": 1360, "tokens_total": 155, "cost": 0.000039, "…": "…" } ], "total": 1 }

There is no offset. To page, pass the oldest started_at you received as to on the next call.

docs.title: Useful queries
docs.text:
-- Cost per proxy app, last 7 days
SELECT proxy_app_id, model_used, sum(cost) AS cost, count(*) AS requests
FROM telemetry.proxy_traces
WHERE started_at >= now() - interval '7 days' AND status = 'success'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY cost DESC;

-- p95 latency per model, today
SELECT model_used, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) AS p95_ms
FROM telemetry.proxy_traces
WHERE started_at >= date_trunc('day', now()) AND status = 'success'
GROUP BY 1;

-- Why requests were denied
SELECT denial_reason, count(*) FROM telemetry.proxy_traces
WHERE status = 'denied' AND started_at >= now() - interval '1 day'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

-- Everything a given user did (x-axium-user-id)
SELECT started_at, surface, model_used, tokens_total, cost, status
FROM telemetry.proxy_traces WHERE client_user_id = 'user-42' ORDER BY started_at DESC;

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
Axium never deletes traces. Add your own job. The started_at index makes range deletes cheap:

DELETE FROM telemetry.proxy_traces WHERE started_at < now() - interval '365 days';

For large volumes convert the table to monthly partitions (pg_partman or native declarative partitioning) and drop old partitions instead. Axium only runs INSERTs against the table name, so partitioning is transparent to it.

client_ip is personal data under most privacy regimes; include the table in your data-retention and subject-access procedures, or null the column after a short period:

UPDATE telemetry.proxy_traces SET client_ip = NULL
WHERE started_at < now() - interval '30 days' AND client_ip IS NOT NULL;

docs.title: Startup sequence
docs.text:
What the core does when it starts, in order. Useful for reading logs:

  1. License check against the Axium Lab service. Never blocks.
  2. Database connection, retried every second for 30 s, then the process exits.
  3. Schema: install, migrate or verify. A failed migration exits; a failed first install keeps the process up so /v1/install/status can be queried.
  4. Telemetry snapshot (once, in the background).
  5. Observability destination start (in the background; never delays the port).
  6. Listen on PORT.

docs.title: Shutdown
docs.text: SIGTERM or SIGINT: stop accepting connections, finish in-flight requests (streams included), close the database pool, flush the observability buffer, exit 0. After 10 s it forces exit 1. Give containers at least 15 s of grace.

docs.title: Known limitations in this version
docs.text:
For planning, not surprises:

  • Rate limits (rate_limit_rpm, rate_limit_tpm), the fallback model, firewall.outbound, dlp_file and capture are stored but not enforced.
  • Observability traces have no built-in retention; batches are not retried.
  • Streamed responses and uploads are held in memory until complete.
  • No Anthropic dialect, no embeddings, images or audio endpoints.
  • The license is validated but not enforced.
  • Latency and error counters in daily statistics stay at zero; use traces.
  • POST /v1/install is public; restrict it at the ingress.

docs.title: Backup & restore
docs.text:
Axium keeps all its state in PostgreSQL. Neither the core nor the ui write to disk, so a complete backup is the database plus the master key.

A backup without the master key is incomplete

Provider credentials are stored encrypted with MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY. A restored database with a different key starts fine, but every provider fails to authenticate until its credentials are entered again. Store the key with the backups, in a separate secret store, with the same retention.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Logical dump with pg_dump, which works across PostgreSQL minor versions and is easy to inspect:

docker exec axium-db pg_dump -U axium -Fc axium-api > axium-$(date +%F).dump

Restore into an empty database:

docker exec -i axium-db pg_restore -U axium -d axium-api --clean --if-exists < axium-2026-10-19.dump

Stop the core while restoring, then start it again. It detects the installed schema and does not reinstall anything.

Alternatively, snapshot the volume with the database stopped:

docker stop axium-core axium-db
docker run --rm -v axium-pgdata:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
  tar czf /backup/axium-pgdata-$(date +%F).tgz -C /data .
docker start axium-db axium-core

docs.title: Google Cloud
docs.text:
The installer creates the Cloud SQL instance with --no-backup to keep the pilot cheap. For production enable automated backups and point-in-time recovery:

gcloud sql instances patch axium-db \
  --backup-start-time=03:00 \
  --enable-point-in-time-recovery \
  --retained-backups-count=14

Take an on-demand backup before an upgrade:

gcloud sql backups create --instance=axium-db

The master key is in the Cloud Run service configuration. Read it back with:

gcloud run services describe axium-core --region europe-west1 \
  --format='value(spec.template.spec.containers[0].env)'

and store it in Secret Manager or your password manager.

docs.title: What to test
docs.text:
A backup you have not restored is a hypothesis. Once a quarter, restore the latest dump into a scratch database, start a core against it with the production master key and check that:

  • GET /v1/install/status answers installed.
  • A request through a proxy app reaches the provider, which proves the credentials decrypt.

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text:
The core exposes three signals. Use the right one for the question you are asking.

Endpoint Auth Touches the DB Answers the question GET /v1/health none no Is the process alive and listening? GET /v1/install/status none yes Is the schema installed and can the database be reached? GET /v1/diagnostics bearer yes (tolerates failure) What version is running, what schema does it see, is observability on?

docs.title: /v1/health
docs.text:
{"status":"ok"}

Always 200 while the process runs, even if the schema failed to install or the database is down. Use it for liveness only.

docs.title: /v1/install/status
docs.text:
{"status":true,"data":{"state":"installed","version":3}}
state Meaning What to do installed Schema present; version is its version. The healthy answer. Nothing. not_installed Empty database. The core installs on its own at startup; seeing this after startup means the install failed. docker logs axium-core \| grep '\[install\]'. Usually a permissions problem (permission denied for database). partial Axium schemas exist but no version table. A previous install died halfway. Inspect by hand. On a fresh install, drop the core, llm, rm and stats schemas and restart. error / no answer Database unreachable. Check DATABASE_URL, network, credentials.

Use it for readiness: a replica that cannot reach the database should not receive traffic. It is cheap, but it is a real query; probe every 10 to 30 s, not every second.

docs.title: /v1/diagnostics
docs.text:
curl -s http://localhost:3000/v1/diagnostics -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

{
  "version": "3.1.0",
  "db_schema": { "state": "installed", "version": 3, "expected": 3 },
  "observability": { "enabled": true, "type": "postgres" }
}

With the database down db_schema becomes {"state":"unreachable","expected":3} and the route still answers 200. Good for a support ticket.

docs.title: Built into the image
docs.text: The core image declares its own Docker HEALTHCHECK: every 30 s, 5 s timeout, 3 retries, 40 s start period, a GET /v1/health performed with the embedded runtime (no curl or wget in the image). docker ps shows healthy once it passes.

docs.title: Probes by platform
docs.text:
Docker ComposeKubernetesCloud RunExternal monitor 
core:
  healthcheck:
    test: ["CMD", "bun", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/v1/install/status').then(r => r.json()).then(j => process.exit(j.data.state === 'installed' ? 0 : 1)).catch(() => process.exit(1))"]
    interval: 15s
    timeout: 5s
    start_period: 60s
    retries: 5

The image has no curl or wget; bun -e is the available HTTP client.

livenessProbe:
  httpGet: { path: /v1/health, port: 3000 }
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 15
readinessProbe:
  httpGet: { path: /v1/install/status, port: 3000 }
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 20
  failureThreshold: 3
startupProbe:
  httpGet: { path: /v1/health, port: 3000 }
  periodSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 12        # 60 s for the DB wait + install
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 20

The readiness probe treats any 200 as ready, so a not_installed answer also passes. If you want the state checked, use an exec probe with the bun -e one-liner from the Compose tab.

Cloud Run uses the container's listening port as the startup signal. Add a startup probe on /v1/health if cold starts are slow:

gcloud run services update axium-core --region europe-west1 \
  --startup-probe=httpGet.path=/v1/health,httpGet.port=3000,periodSeconds=5,failureThreshold=12

Alert on GET https://axium-api.your-domain.com/v1/install/status not containing "state":"installed". That single check covers process, network, database and schema.

docs.title: The ui
docs.text: No endpoint. A 200 on / means the static server is up. Whether the console can reach the API depends on API_URL and is decided in the user's browser; test it by logging in.

docs.title: The core is stateless
docs.text:
Every piece of state lives in PostgreSQL: sessions, API keys, cache, counters. Installation and migrations take an advisory lock, so any number of replicas can start simultaneously. Run as many core replicas as you need behind any load balancer, with no sticky sessions.

The one per-process thing is the observability buffer (up to 10,000 traces, flushed every 2 s). A replica killed without SIGTERM loses what was in it.

docs.title: What uses memory
docs.text:
Driver Size Control File upload in flight Up to MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE (50 MB) each, fully in RAM Lower MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE; cap concurrency Streamed response in flight The whole response, until it ends Cap concurrency JSON body Up to 10 MB each Fixed Observability buffer ≤ 10,000 traces, roughly 1 KB each Fixed Baseline ~100 MB

Rule of thumb: baseline + concurrency × typical request footprint. The GCP installer's choice of 1 GiB with concurrency 20 assumes chat traffic with occasional uploads. For an upload-heavy workload either give 2 GiB+ or lower the concurrency per replica and add replicas.

CPU is rarely the limit: the core forwards bytes and parses JSON. DLP scanning of very large prompts is the heaviest CPU path.

docs.title: Connection budget
docs.text:
Each core replica opens:

Pool Max connections Main (DATABASE_URL) 10 Observability (OBSERVABILITY_DB_POSTGRESQL) 8

replicas × 18 must fit under PostgreSQL's max_connections with room for administrators and backups. Beyond a handful of replicas, put PgBouncer in transaction mode in front of the database.

docs.title: Kubernetes manifest
docs.text:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: axium-core }
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: axium-core } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: axium-core } }
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 20
      imagePullSecrets: [ { name: quay } ]
      containers:
        - name: core
          image: quay.io/axiumlab/core:v0.1.0
          ports: [ { containerPort: 3000 } ]
          env:
            - { name: TRUST_PROXY, value: "true" }
            - { name: PUBLIC_BASE_URL, value: https://axium-api.your-domain.com }
            - { name: OBSERVABILITY_TYPE, value: postgres }
          envFrom:
            - secretRef: { name: axium-core }   # DATABASE_URL, MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY, AXIUM_LICENSE, OBSERVABILITY_DB_POSTGRESQL
          resources:
            requests: { cpu: 250m, memory: 512Mi }
            limits:   { memory: 1Gi }
          livenessProbe:  { httpGet: { path: /v1/health, port: 3000 }, periodSeconds: 15 }
          readinessProbe: { httpGet: { path: /v1/install/status, port: 3000 }, periodSeconds: 20 }
          startupProbe:   { httpGet: { path: /v1/health, port: 3000 }, periodSeconds: 5, failureThreshold: 12 }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: { name: axium-core }
spec:
  selector: { app: axium-core }
  ports: [ { port: 80, targetPort: 3000 } ]

Autoscale on CPU or, better, on concurrent requests at the ingress. Keep the ui at one or two replicas; it serves static files.

docs.title: Cloud Run
docs.text:
The installer deploys with --memory 1Gi --cpu 1 --concurrency 20 --min-instances 0 --max-instances 4. Adjust with:

gcloud run services update axium-core --region europe-west1 \
  --min-instances 1 --max-instances 10 --concurrency 20 --memory 2Gi --timeout 900

--min-instances 1 removes cold starts (and the schema check they repeat). Remember the Cloud SQL tier: db-f1-micro allows few connections; move to a dedicated-core tier before scaling the core past two or three instances.

docs.title: Database growth
docs.text: Table Grows with Keep in check stats.proxy_daily apps × models × keys × days Small; no action. rm.request_io cached responses DELETE …/cache/expired on a schedule. telemetry.proxy_traces one row per request Your retention job or partitioning.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptoms first, then the cause and the fix. Start every investigation with:

curl -s http://<core>/v1/install/status
docker logs axium-core 2>&1 | grep -E '^\[(install|db|license|observability|errorHandler)\]'

docs.title: Startup
Console
docs.text:
The login page shows a network error

The browser cannot reach API_URL. Open the browser's developer tools:

  • Mixed content blocked: the ui is https:// and API_URL is http://. Use https://.
  • Name not resolved: API_URL uses an internal name (http://axium-core:3000/v1). It must be a URL the browser can reach.
  • CORS error: usually a proxy in front of the core stripping headers or answering the pre-flight itself. The core allows all origins; let OPTIONS requests through.
  • 404 on login: API_URL is missing the /v1 suffix or has a trailing slash.
Invalid email or password with the initial credentials

The user was already changed, or the database was restored from another installation. Reset with an administrator account, or, if none is available, with SQL against core.users (ask support for the procedure).

Providers fail after a restore or a redeploy

MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY differs from the one the credentials were encrypted with. Recover the original key. If it is gone, edit each provider and enter its credentials again.

docs.title: Runtime (SDK traffic)
docs.text:
401 from the gateway

The key is unknown, inactive or expired; all three answer the same. Check the key in the console (GET /v1/rm/api-keys), its expires_at, and that the SDK actually sends it: the OpenAI SDK as Authorization: Bearer, Google's as x-goog-api-key. A ?key= query parameter is ignored.

403 from the gateway

Read the error message and the trace's denial_reason:

Message / reason Fix key of another app, scope mismatch Use a key created for this proxy app. app_not_ready Publish the app (PATCH /v1/proxy-apps/:id/publish) or reactivate it. model_not_allowed Add the model to the app's allow-list, or fix the name. provider_inactive Activate the provider. firewall_denied Client IP not allowed. Behind a proxy, set TRUST_PROXY=true or every client looks like the proxy. dlp_blocked The prompt contained data the policy blocks. 404 Route not found from the Vertex gateway in Java

The SDK entered Vertex express mode because it was given .apiKey() alone and changed the path to /v1/publishers/…. Pass the key as a static credential instead; see SDK examples.

429 from the gateway

Either the provider's own rate limit relayed verbatim (error_origin: provider) or the app's budget (denial_reason: budget_exhausted). Raise budget_limit, wait for the period to roll over, or check the provider's quota.

Streaming arrives all at once at the end

Something in front buffers the response. Disable proxy buffering (nginx proxy_buffering off, Caddy flush_interval -1). The core already sends X-Accel-Buffering: no.

Uploads fail with 413 or a connection reset

Three limits apply: the reverse proxy's body size, MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE (default 50 MB), and the container's memory, since uploads are buffered in RAM. Align all three.

Gemini resumable upload: the second request goes to the wrong host

Set PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://axium-api.your-domain.com and TRUST_PROXY=true so the upload URL handed back points through Axium with the right scheme.

403 PERMISSION_DENIED … aiplatform.endpoints.predict on Google Cloud

The core's service account lacks roles/aiplatform.user in the project configured on the provider. Re-run gcp.sh or update.sh with VERTEX_PROJECT=<that project>, or grant the role by hand.

Cost is null in traces and statistics

The model has no prices configured. Set input and output price per million tokens on the model.

docs.title: Collecting information for support
docs.text:
curl -s http://<core>/v1/diagnostics -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
docker logs --since 1h axium-core 2>&1 | grep -vE '^\[(req|runtime|usage)\]'

Plus the x-axium-trace-id of a failing request, which identifies its trace.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: The containers are disposable and the PostgreSQL volume is the only state, so an upgrade is "pull the new image, replace the container". What needs care is the schema policy described at the end of this page.

docs.title: Before you upgrade
docs.text:
• You have a database backup taken after the last change you care about (Backup & restore).
  • You have the master key stored outside the deployment.
  • You have read the release notes of every version between yours and the target, especially for a new major.
  • You know the current version: GET /v1/install/status reports the schema version (Health checks).

docs.title: With Docker
docs.text:
docker pull quay.io/axiumlab/core:v0.2.0
docker stop axium-core && docker rm axium-core
# relaunch the docker run from the install guide with the new tag

Same for the ui. With Compose, change the tag in .env and run docker compose pull && docker compose up -d.

Upgrade the core first, then the ui: the console consumes the API, not the other way round.

docs.title: On Google Cloud
docs.text:
infra-gcp/update.sh upgrades the core, the ui or both on an installation created by gcp.sh:

wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/axium-lab/infrastructure-documentation/refs/heads/main/infra-gcp/update.sh \
  && chmod +x update.sh

bash update.sh                  # asks what to upgrade
bash update.sh core             # only the core
bash update.sh ui               # only the ui
TAG=v0.2.0 bash update.sh both  # both, on a specific version (recommended)

What it does:

  1. Checks that the services and the Artifact Registry repository exist. If not, it stops and points you at gcp.sh.
  2. When the core is included, re-applies the APIs and IAM roles the core needs (Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, Vertex AI). Installations created by an older installer lack some of them, and without them the new core starts but answers 403 as soon as it touches a bucket or a Google model. Every binding is idempotent and none aborts the upgrade: without IAM permission the script warns and prints the command for whoever has it. SKIP_IAM=1 skips the step.
  3. Resolves the digest of the tag on Quay, copies the image by digest to Artifact Registry and deploys that exact digest. With latest this removes the window in which the tag could move between copy and deploy.
  4. Redeploys passing only --image. Cloud Run keeps everything else: environment variables, the Cloud SQL attachment, memory, concurrency and IAM. The script never reads or rewrites MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY or API_URL.
  5. Verifies /v1/install/status on the core and a 200 on the ui root.

Options: REGION= if you did not deploy to europe-west1, VERTEX_PROJECT= if Vertex AI lives in another project, DEBUG=1 for registry diagnostics.

docs.title: Rolling back on Cloud Run
docs.text:
Every deploy creates a revision. To send traffic back to the previous one:

gcloud run revisions list --service axium-core --region europe-west1
gcloud run services update-traffic axium-core --region europe-west1 \
  --to-revisions <previous-revision>=100

docs.title: Schema policy
docs.text:
Each image ships a schema version. At startup the core compares it with the database:

Database Action Same version Nothing. Older The bundled migrations are applied automatically, one version at a time, each in its own transaction and under an advisory lock, so several replicas can start together. Log: [install] schema migrated 1 -> 3. Newer The process exits: The database is at schema version N but this build ships M. Update the API to the latest version. Schema never downgrades, so rolling back an image after a migration is not supported without restoring the database.

A failed migration exits the process instead of serving an unknown schema. That is why the backup comes first in the checklist above.

Major versions

Minor and patch releases keep migrations small and backward compatible. A new major may carry migrations that are expensive on a large database or that change behaviour. Read the release notes and, if in doubt, ask Axium Lab before moving up a major version.

If after an upgrade /v1/install/status reports anything other than installed, or the core exits on start, restore the backup, roll back the image and contact support with the output of:

docker logs axium-core | grep '\[install\]'
